questions.q: Which TWO words apply to nitrogen (N₂)?

why.en: N₂ has only ONE capital letter (N), so only one kind of atom: an element. Nitrogen boils at about −196 °C, far below room temperature, so it is a gas (it makes up 78% of air).
why.zh: N₂ 只有一个大写字母（N），只有一种原子：单质。氮气的沸点约 −196 °C，远低于室温，所以是气体（占空气的 78%）。

gas, compound.en: Gas is right, but a compound needs two DIFFERENT elements. N₂ is only nitrogen.
gas, compound.zh: 气体对了，但化合物需要两种不同元素。N₂ 只有氮。

solid, mixture.en: Nitrogen is a gas at room temperature, and N₂ is one pure substance, not a mixture.
solid, mixture.zh: 氮在室温下是气体，N₂ 是一种纯净物，不是混合物。

liquid, element.en: Element is right, but nitrogen is a GAS at room temperature. It is only liquid below −196 °C.
liquid, element.zh: 单质对了，但氮在室温下是气体，只有低于 −196 °C 才是液体。

questions.qzh: 哪两个词适用于氮气（N₂）？

questions.q: Which statement is TRUE?
options: There are 2 liquid elements at room temperature.

why.en: At room temperature only 2 elements are liquids: mercury (a metal) and bromine (a non-metal). Every other element is a solid or a gas.
why.zh: 室温下只有 2 种元素是液体：汞（金属）和溴（非金属）。其他元素都是固体或气体。

Most elements are non-metals..en: About three quarters of the elements are METALS (the whole left and middle of the periodic table).
Most elements are non-metals..zh: 大约四分之三的元素是金属（周期表的左边和中间）。

Most metals are magnetic..en: Only iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic. Most metals (copper, gold, aluminium) are not.
Most metals are magnetic..zh: 只有铁、镍、钴有磁性。大多数金属（铜、金、铝）没有。

There are about 1000 elements..en: There are about 118 known elements, not 1000.
There are about 1000 elements..zh: 已知的元素约 118 种，不是 1000 种。

questions.qzh: 哪一句是对的？

ozh.There are 2 liquid elements at room temp: 室温下有 2 种液态元素。

questions.q: Gas → liquid is called...

why.en: Cooling a gas turns it back to liquid: condensing.
why.zh: 气体冷却变回液体：凝结。

boiling.en: Boiling is the opposite: liquid → gas.
boiling.zh: 沸腾正相反：液体 → 气体。

questions.qzh: 气体 → 液体叫……

questions.q: In the metal-heating test, what is the ONE thing you change?

why.en: A fair test changes only ONE thing, the independent variable, so you know that thing caused the result. Here you change the TYPE of metal and keep everything else the same.
why.zh: 公平测试只改变一样东西（自变量），这样才知道结果是它造成的。这里改变的是金属的种类，其他都保持不变。

the mass after heating.en: The mass after heating is what you MEASURE (the dependent variable), the result.
the mass after heating.zh: 加热后的质量是你测量的东西（因变量），是结果。

the colour of the flame.en: The flame is not what is being tested, and changing it would make the test unfair.
the colour of the flame.zh: 火焰不是要测试的东西，改变它会让测试不公平。

the change in mass.en: The change in mass is the RESULT you work out, not something you choose.
the change in mass.zh: 质量变化是你算出来的结果，不是你选的。

questions.qzh: 在加热金属的实验里，你只改变的那一样是什么？

questions.q: The mass went UP after heating. Who is right?

why.en: Mass up = the metal gained oxygen from the air. That supports Lavoisier only.
why.zh: 质量增加 = 金属从空气中得到了氧。只支持 Lavoisier。

Priestley.en: Priestley's idea (phlogiston) said metals LOSE something when heated, so the mass should go DOWN. It went up.
Priestley.zh: 普里斯特利的理论（燃素）说金属加热会失去东西，质量应该下降。结果质量上升了。

both.en: Their ideas predict opposite results (mass up vs mass down), so the evidence cannot support both.
both.zh: 他们的理论预测相反的结果（质量上升和下降），证据不可能同时支持两个人。

neither.en: The mass going up fits Lavoisier's idea: the metal joined with oxygen from the air.
neither.zh: 质量上升符合拉瓦锡的理论：金属和空气中的氧结合了。

questions.qzh: 加热后质量增加了。谁说得对？

questions.q: Ratio of carbon : oxygen in CO₂?

why.en: Read the formula: CO₂ = 1 carbon (no number means 1) and 2 oxygens. Write the ratio in the same order as the question: carbon : oxygen = 1 : 2.
why.zh: 看化学式：CO₂ = 1 个碳（没写数字就是 1）和 2 个氧。按题目的顺序写比：碳 : 氧 = 1 : 2。

2 : 1.en: This is oxygen : carbon, the wrong order. The question asks carbon first.
2 : 1.zh: 这是氧 : 碳，顺序反了。题目要碳在前。

1 : 1.en: That would be CO (carbon monoxide). The small 2 means two oxygens.
1 : 1.zh: 那是 CO（一氧化碳）。小的 2 表示两个氧。

3 : 1.en: There are 3 atoms in TOTAL, but the ratio compares carbon (1) with oxygen (2).
3 : 1.zh: 总共有 3 个原子，但比是碳（1）比氧（2）。

questions.qzh: CO₂ 里碳 : 氧的比是多少？

questions.q: How many OXYGEN atoms are in 6 molecules of CO₂?

why.en: Each CO₂ molecule has 2 oxygen atoms. 6 molecules × 2 oxygens each = 12 oxygen atoms.
why.zh: 每个 CO₂ 分子有 2 个氧原子。6 个分子 × 每个 2 个氧 = 12 个氧原子。

2.en: 2 is the oxygens in ONE molecule. There are 6 molecules.
2.zh: 2 是一个分子里的氧。这里有 6 个分子。

6.en: 6 is the number of molecules. Each one has 2 oxygens, so multiply.
6.zh: 6 是分子数。每个有 2 个氧，要相乘。

18.en: 18 is 6 × 3, counting ALL the atoms (C and O). The question asks only for oxygen.
18.zh: 18 是 6 × 3，把所有原子（C 和 O）都算了。题目只问氧。

questions.qzh: 6 个 CO₂ 分子里有几个氧原子？

questions.q: 24 + x = 40. What is x?

why.en: Undo "24 +" by subtracting 24 from both sides: x = 40 − 24 = 16. Check: 24 + 16 = 40 ✓.

64.en: 64 is 40 + 24: it adds instead of undoing. Check: 24 + 64 = 88.

questions.qzh: 24 + x = 40。x 等于多少？

questions.q: Simplify the ratio 6 : 9.

why.en: Simplify a ratio by dividing BOTH sides by the same number, the biggest that goes into both (the HCF). 3 goes into 6 and 9: 6 ÷ 3 = 2, 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so 2 : 3.
why.zh: 化简比要把两边除以同一个数，用能同时整除的最大数（最大公因数）。3 能整除 6 和 9：6 ÷ 3 = 2，9 ÷ 3 = 3，所以是 2 : 3。

3 : 2.en: This swaps the order. The 6 came first, so its part (2) comes first.
3 : 2.zh: 这把顺序换了。6 在前面，所以它的 2 在前面。

1 : 3.en: 1 : 3 is the same as 3 : 9, not 6 : 9. Both sides must be divided by the same number.
1 : 3.zh: 1 : 3 等于 3 : 9，不等于 6 : 9。两边要除以同一个数。

6 : 3.en: Only the 9 was divided. Divide BOTH sides by 3.

questions.qzh: 化简比 6 : 9。

questions.q: In a results table, what goes in the FIRST column?

why.en: The first column is always what you change.
why.zh: 第一列永远是你改变的东西。

change in mass (g).en: The change in mass is a RESULT, so it goes in a later column (usually the last).
change in mass (g).zh: 质量变化是结果，放在后面的列（通常是最后一列）。

mass after (g).en: Mass after is a MEASUREMENT, which goes after the column of what you change.
mass after (g).zh: 加热后的质量是测量值，放在改变量那一列的后面。

your name.en: Your name is not data. Tables only hold the variables.
your name.zh: 名字不是数据，表格里只放变量。

questions.qzh: 在结果表里，第一列放什么？

ozh.what you change (type of metal): 你改变的东西（金属种类）

questions.q: Air is a...

why.en: A mixture has two or more substances that are together but NOT chemically joined, and it can be separated. Air is nitrogen, oxygen, argon and carbon dioxide all mixed, each keeping its own properties.
why.zh: 混合物是两种或更多物质在一起，但没有化学结合，可以分开。空气是氮气、氧气、氩气和二氧化碳混在一起，各自保持自己的性质。

element.en: An element has only ONE kind of atom. Air has several different gases.
element.zh: 单质只有一种原子。空气里有好几种不同的气体。

compound.en: In a compound the atoms are chemically JOINED with a fixed formula. Air has no single formula and its gases are not joined.
compound.zh: 化合物的原子是化学结合的，有固定的化学式。空气没有一个化学式，里面的气体没有结合。

molecule.en: A molecule is just two or more atoms joined. It is not one of the three kinds of substance (element, compound, mixture). Always name the kind of substance.
molecule.zh: 分子只是两个或更多原子连在一起，不是三种物质类型（单质、化合物、混合物）之一。要写出物质的类型。

questions.qzh: 空气是一种……

questions.q: Sodium chloride (NaCl) is a...

why.en: A compound is two or more DIFFERENT elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. NaCl has two capital letters (Na, Cl), so two elements, joined 1 : 1.
why.zh: 化合物是两种或更多不同的元素按固定比例化学结合。NaCl 有两个大写字母（Na、Cl），是两种元素，按 1 : 1 结合。

element.en: An element has only ONE capital letter in its formula. NaCl has two: Na and Cl.
element.zh: 单质的化学式只有一个大写字母。NaCl 有两个：Na 和 Cl。

mixture.en: A mixture is not joined and has no formula. NaCl has a formula, so the atoms are joined.
mixture.zh: 混合物没有结合，也没有化学式。NaCl 有化学式，所以原子是结合的。

molecule.en: A molecule is just two or more atoms joined. It is not one of the three kinds of substance (element, compound, mixture). Always name the kind of substance.
molecule.zh: 分子只是两个或更多原子连在一起，不是三种物质类型（单质、化合物、混合物）之一。要写出物质的类型。

questions.qzh: 氯化钠（NaCl）是一种……

questions.q: Brass is a...

why.en: Brass is an ALLOY: copper and zinc melted and mixed together, but not chemically joined, and the amounts can vary. Alloys are mixtures.
why.zh: 黄铜是合金：铜和锌熔化后混在一起，但没有化学结合，而且比例可以变化。合金是混合物。

element.en: Brass contains TWO elements (copper and zinc), so it is not an element.
element.zh: 黄铜有两种元素（铜和锌），所以不是单质。

compound.en: A compound has a fixed formula. Brass can have different amounts of copper and zinc, so it is not a compound.
compound.zh: 化合物有固定的化学式。黄铜里铜和锌的比例可以不同，所以不是化合物。

molecule.en: A molecule is just two or more atoms joined. It is not one of the three kinds of substance (element, compound, mixture). Always name the kind of substance.
molecule.zh: 分子只是两个或更多原子连在一起，不是三种物质类型（单质、化合物、混合物）之一。要写出物质的类型。

questions.qzh: 黄铜是一种……

questions.q: Which TWO words describe nitrogen (N₂) at room temperature?

why.en: N₂ has only ONE capital letter (N), so only one kind of atom: an element. Nitrogen boils at about −196 °C, far below room temperature, so it is a gas (it makes up 78% of air).
why.zh: N₂ 只有一个大写字母（N），只有一种原子：单质。氮气的沸点约 −196 °C，远低于室温，所以是气体（占空气的 78%）。

gas, compound.en: Gas is right, but a compound needs two DIFFERENT elements. N₂ is only nitrogen.
gas, compound.zh: 气体对了，但化合物需要两种不同元素。N₂ 只有氮。

solid, mixture.en: Nitrogen is a gas at room temperature, and N₂ is one pure substance, not a mixture.
solid, mixture.zh: 氮在室温下是气体，N₂ 是一种纯净物，不是混合物。

liquid, element.en: Element is right, but nitrogen is a GAS at room temperature. It is only liquid below −196 °C.
liquid, element.zh: 单质对了，但氮在室温下是气体，只有低于 −196 °C 才是液体。

questions.qzh: 哪两个词描述室温下的氮气（N₂）？

questions.q: How is pure bromine (Br₂) classified as a substance?

why.en: Bromine contains only bromine atoms, so it is an element. Each Br₂ molecule has two bromine atoms. An element can be made of molecules.
why.zh: 溴只含溴原子，所以是元素。每个 Br₂ 分子含两个溴原子。元素也可以由分子构成。

compound.en: A compound needs at least two DIFFERENT elements. Br₂ is two atoms of the SAME element.
compound.zh: 化合物至少要两种不同的元素。Br₂ 是两个同种原子。

mixture of elements.en: Pure bromine has only ONE substance, so it cannot be a mixture.
mixture of elements.zh: 纯溴只有一种物质，不可能是混合物。

mixture of compounds.en: There are no compounds here, and pure means only one substance.
mixture of compounds.zh: 这里没有化合物，而且纯净就是只有一种物质。

questions.qzh: 纯溴（Br₂）属于哪一类物质？

questions.q: Iron sulfide is a...

why.en: After heating, iron and sulfur are chemically joined. A magnet cannot pull the iron out. It is a compound.
why.zh: 加热后铁和硫化学结合，磁铁吸不出铁，所以是化合物。

element.en: Iron sulfide has two elements (Fe and S) joined, so it is not an element.
element.zh: 硫化亚铁有两种元素（Fe 和 S）结合，所以不是单质。

mixture.en: Before heating it was a mixture. Heating JOINED them chemically, so a magnet can no longer separate them.
mixture.zh: 加热前是混合物。加热让它们化学结合了，所以磁铁再也分不开。

molecule.en: A molecule is just two or more atoms joined. It is not one of the three kinds of substance (element, compound, mixture). Always name the kind of substance.
molecule.zh: 分子只是两个或更多原子连在一起，不是三种物质类型（单质、化合物、混合物）之一。要写出物质的类型。

questions.qzh: 硫化亚铁是一种……

questions.q: Petrol is a...

why.en: Petrol has no single formula. It is many things mixed together: a mixture.
why.zh: 汽油没有一个化学式，是很多东西混在一起：混合物。

element.en: Petrol contains many different substances, not one kind of atom.
element.zh: 汽油里有很多不同的物质，不是一种原子。

compound.en: A compound has one fixed formula. Petrol has none, because it is many compounds mixed.
compound.zh: 化合物有一个固定的化学式。汽油没有，因为它是很多化合物混在一起。

molecule.en: A molecule is just two or more atoms joined. It is not one of the three kinds of substance (element, compound, mixture). Always name the kind of substance.
molecule.zh: 分子只是两个或更多原子连在一起，不是三种物质类型（单质、化合物、混合物）之一。要写出物质的类型。

questions.qzh: 汽油是一种……

questions.q: Which formula is an ELEMENT?

why.en: Count the CAPITAL letters: each one is a different element. O₂ has one capital letter, so only one kind of atom: an element. (The small 2 just means two O atoms are joined.)
why.zh: 数大写字母：每个大写字母是一种元素。O₂ 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子：单质。（小的 2 只表示两个 O 原子连在一起。）

NaCl.en: Two capital letters (Na, Cl): two elements joined, a compound.
NaCl.zh: 两个大写字母（Na、Cl）：两种元素结合，是化合物。

H₂O.en: Two capital letters (H, O): two elements joined, a compound.
H₂O.zh: 两个大写字母（H、O）：两种元素结合，是化合物。

CO₂.en: Two capital letters (C, O): two elements joined, a compound.
CO₂.zh: 两个大写字母（C、O）：两种元素结合，是化合物。

questions.qzh: 哪个化学式是单质？

questions.q: A box has blue-blue molecules and single red atoms, not joined to each other. What is the FULL name?

why.en: Blue-blue = an element (same atoms). Red atoms = another element. Two elements, not joined. Always write the FULL name in a test.
why.zh: 蓝蓝 = 一种元素，红原子 = 另一种元素，没有结合。考试要写完整的名称。

mixture.en: Correct idea but not the FULL name. Tests want what is mixed: two elements.
mixture.zh: 思路对了，但不是完整的名称。考试要写出混合的是什么：两种单质。

mixture of two compounds.en: A compound needs DIFFERENT atoms joined. Blue-blue is the same atoms, and the red atoms are single, so both are elements.
mixture of two compounds.zh: 化合物需要不同的原子结合。蓝-蓝是同种原子，红色是单个原子，所以两者都是单质。

compound.en: In a compound the different atoms are JOINED. Here blue and red are not joined to each other.
compound.zh: 化合物里不同的原子是结合的。这里蓝和红没有连在一起。

questions.qzh: 一个盒子里有“蓝-蓝”分子和单个的红色原子，彼此没有连在一起。它的完整名称是什么？

questions.q: A box has only blue-blue molecules. What is the FULL name?

why.en: Every particle is the same, and each one is the same atoms joined. Write "element (molecules)", not just "molecules".
why.zh: 每个粒子都一样，都是相同的原子结合。要写 element (molecules)，不能只写 molecules。

molecules.en: "Molecules" only says atoms are joined; it does not name the substance. Tests want the full name: element (molecules).
molecules.zh: molecules 只说原子连在一起，没有说出物质类型。考试要完整名称：element (molecules)。

compound.en: A compound needs DIFFERENT atoms joined. These are the same atoms (blue-blue).
compound.zh: 化合物要不同的原子结合。这里是同种原子（蓝-蓝）。

mixture.en: A mixture needs at least two different substances. Every particle here is the same.
mixture.zh: 混合物至少要两种不同的物质。这里每个粒子都一样。

questions.qzh: 一个盒子里只有“蓝-蓝”分子。它的完整名称是什么？

canNow.en: I can now fix the tricky questions by myself.
canNow.zh: 我现在能自己改正难题。

intro.zh: 读关键词，用自己的话说出意思，再点卡片检查。

cards.back: A disturbance that transfers energy from one place to another.
cards.zhBack: 把能量从一个地方传到另一个地方的扰动。

cards.back: A wave in which vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of travel.
cards.zhBack: 振动方向和传播方向垂直的波。

cards.back: A wave in which vibrations are parallel to the direction of travel.
cards.zhBack: 振动方向和传播方向平行的波。

cards.back: The maximum distance a point on a wave moves from its resting position.
cards.zhBack: 波上一点离开静止位置的最大距离。

cards.back: The distance between two corresponding points on consecutive waves, such as crest to crest.
cards.zhBack: 相邻两个波上对应两点之间的距离，例如波峰到波峰。

cards.back: The number of complete waves passing a point each second.
cards.zhBack: 每秒经过某一点的完整波的数量。

cards.back: The unit used to measure frequency. One hertz equals one wave per second.
cards.zhBack: 频率的单位。1 赫兹 = 每秒 1 个波。

cards.back: A substance or material through which a wave travels.
cards.zhBack: 波在其中传播的物质或材料。

cards.back: A repeated movement backwards and forwards around a resting position.
cards.zhBack: 在静止位置附近来回重复的运动。

cards.back: A space containing no particles.
cards.zhBack: 没有任何粒子的空间。

cards.back: A region of a longitudinal wave where particles are close together.
cards.zhBack: 纵波中粒子挤在一起的区域。

cards.back: A region of a longitudinal wave where particles are spread further apart.
cards.zhBack: 纵波中粒子分得更开的区域。

canNow.en: I can now explain the 12 wave keywords.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释 12 个关于波的关键词。

intro.en: Read the keyword, say the meaning in your own words, then tap to check.
intro.zh: 读关键词，用自己的话说出意思，再点卡片检查。

cards.back: How high or low a sound seems. It depends on the frequency of the sound wave.
cards.zhBack: 声音听起来有多高或多低，取决于声波的频率。

cards.back: How loud or quiet a sound seems. It is related to the amplitude and intensity of the sound wave.
cards.zhBack: 声音听起来有多响或多轻，和声波的振幅、强度有关。

cards.back: The unit used to measure sound level. The decibel scale is logarithmic.
cards.zhBack: 测量声音大小的单位。分贝是对数刻度。

cards.back: The range of sound frequencies that an animal can hear. For humans, this is approximately 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
cards.zhBack: 动物能听到的声音频率范围。人大约是 20 Hz 到 20,000 Hz。

cards.back: Sound with a frequency higher than 20,000 Hz, above the usual human hearing range.
cards.zhBack: 频率高于 20,000 Hz 的声音，高过人的听觉范围。

cards.back: Sound with a frequency lower than 20 Hz, below the usual human hearing range.
cards.zhBack: 频率低于 20 Hz 的声音，低过人的听觉范围。

cards.back: A sound heard again after it has reflected off a surface.
cards.zhBack: 声音碰到表面反射回来后再次被听到。

cards.back: The use of reflected sound waves to detect objects and determine their position or distance.
cards.zhBack: 利用反射回来的声波发现物体，并判断它的位置或距离。

cards.back: A system that uses reflected sound waves to detect objects and measure distances, commonly underwater.
cards.zhBack: 利用反射声波发现物体、测量距离的系统，常用于水下。

cards.back: The visible outer part of the ear that collects sound waves.
cards.zhBack: 耳朵外面看得见的部分，用来收集声波。

cards.back: The tube that carries sound waves from the pinna to the eardrum.
cards.zhBack: 把声波从耳廓送到鼓膜的管道。

cards.back: A thin membrane that vibrates when sound waves reach it.
cards.zhBack: 声波到达时会振动的一层薄膜。

cards.back: Three tiny bones in the middle ear that transmit and amplify vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.
cards.zhBack: 中耳里的三块小骨头，把鼓膜的振动传到内耳并放大。

cards.back: A spiral-shaped structure in the inner ear that converts vibrations into electrical signals.
cards.zhBack: 内耳里螺旋形的结构，把振动变成电信号。

cards.back: The nerve that carries electrical signals from the cochlea to the brain.
cards.zhBack: 把电信号从耳蜗送到大脑的神经。

canNow.en: I can now explain the 15 sound and hearing keywords.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释 15 个关于声音和听觉的关键词。

intro.en: Read the keyword, say the meaning in your own words, then tap to check.
intro.zh: 读关键词，用自己的话说出意思，再点卡片检查。

cards.back: A material that allows light to pass through clearly, so objects can be seen through it.
cards.zhBack: 能让光清楚地通过的材料，可以看清后面的东西。

cards.back: A material that allows light through but scatters it, so objects cannot be seen clearly through it.
cards.zhBack: 能让光通过但会把光散开的材料，看不清后面的东西。

cards.back: A material that does not allow light to pass through it.
cards.zhBack: 不让光通过的材料。

cards.back: An object that produces its own light.
cards.zhBack: 自己能发光的物体。

cards.back: An object that does not produce its own light, but can be seen by light reflected off it.
cards.zhBack: 自己不发光，但能靠反射的光被看见的物体。

cards.back: A straight line used to show the direction in which light travels.
cards.zhBack: 表示光传播方向的直线。

cards.back: A flat mirror with a smooth, reflective surface.
cards.zhBack: 表面平滑、能反光的平的镜子。

cards.back: When an image appears reversed from left to right, as in a plane mirror.
cards.zhBack: 像的左右反过来，就像在平面镜里一样。

cards.back: The change in direction of light when it bounces off a surface.
cards.zhBack: 光碰到表面弹回来时方向的改变。

cards.back: The change in direction of light when it passes between different materials because its speed changes.
cards.zhBack: 光从一种材料进入另一种材料时，因为速度改变而改变方向。

cards.back: The ray of light travelling towards a surface before reflection or refraction.
cards.zhBack: 反射或折射之前，射向表面的光线。

cards.back: The ray of light that bounces off a surface.
cards.zhBack: 从表面弹回来的光线。

cards.back: The angle between the incident ray and the normal.
cards.zhBack: 入射光线和法线之间的夹角。

cards.back: The angle between the reflected ray and the normal.
cards.zhBack: 反射光线和法线之间的夹角。

cards.back: An imaginary line drawn at 90° to a surface at the point where a ray hits it.
cards.zhBack: 在光线射到表面的那一点，画一条和表面成 90° 的假想线。

cards.back: A transparent object, usually made of glass or plastic, that can refract and disperse light.
cards.zhBack: 通常用玻璃或塑料做的透明物体，能折射光并把光分散开。

cards.back: The separation of white light into its different colours.
cards.zhBack: 白光分成各种颜色。

cards.back: A range of different colours or wavelengths, such as the visible spectrum.
cards.zhBack: 一系列不同的颜色或波长，例如可见光谱。

cards.back: To allow something, such as light, to pass through a material.
cards.zhBack: 让光等东西穿过一种材料。

cards.back: To take in energy, such as light, rather than reflecting or transmitting it.
cards.zhBack: 把光等能量吸进去，而不是反射或透射。

cards.back: A colour of light that can be combined with other primary colours to produce a range of colours. For light, these are red, green and blue.
cards.zhBack: 能和其他原色混合出很多颜色的色光。光的三原色是红、绿、蓝。

cards.back: A colour produced by mixing two primary colours of light. These are cyan, magenta and yellow.
cards.zhBack: 两种原色光混合得到的颜色：青色、品红色和黄色。

canNow.en: I can now explain the 22 light keywords.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释 22 个关于光的关键词。

cards.back: A transverse wave that can travel through a vacuum without needing a medium.

items.text: A transverse wave vibrates ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Transverse = at 90° (perpendicular).

items.textzh: 横波的振动方向和传播方向是 ___ 的。

items.text: A longitudinal wave vibrates ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Longitudinal = along the same line (parallel).
why.zh: 纵波 = 在同一条线上（平行）。

items.textzh: 纵波的振动方向和传播方向是 ___ 的。

items.text: Frequency is measured in ___.

why.en: 1 Hz = one wave per second.
why.zh: 1 Hz = 每秒一个波。

items.textzh: 频率的单位是 ___。

items.text: Sound cannot travel through a ___ because there are no particles.

why.en: Sound needs a medium. A vacuum has no particles.
why.zh: 声音需要介质，真空里没有粒子。

items.textzh: 声音不能在 ___ 中传播，因为那里没有粒子。

items.text: In a longitudinal wave, a ___ is where the particles are close together.

why.en: Compression = squashed together.
why.zh: 密部 = 挤在一起。

items.textzh: 在纵波里，___ 是粒子挤在一起的地方。

items.text: The ___ of a sound depends on its frequency.

why.en: High frequency = high pitch.
why.zh: 频率高 = 音调高。

items.textzh: 声音的 ___ 取决于它的频率。

items.text: Sound level is measured in ___.

why.en: The unit is the decibel (dB).
why.zh: 单位是分贝 (dB)。

items.textzh: 声音的大小用 ___ 来测量。

items.text: Humans can hear from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. This is the ___ range.

why.en: Audible = can be heard.
why.zh: audible = 能听到。

items.textzh: 人能听到大约 20 Hz 到 20,000 Hz 的声音。这是人的 ___ 范围。

items.text: Bats find food using ___: they listen for reflected sound.

why.en: Echo + location: using echoes to find where things are.
why.zh: 回声 + 定位：用回声找到东西在哪里。

items.textzh: 蝙蝠用 ___ 找食物：它们听反射回来的声音。

items.text: The ___ is a thin membrane that vibrates when sound reaches it.

why.en: The eardrum passes the vibrations to the ossicles.
why.zh: 鼓膜把振动传给听小骨。

items.textzh: ___ 是一层薄膜，声音传到时会振动。

items.textzh: 磨砂玻璃是 ___ 的：光能透过，但看不清楚。

items.text: The Sun is ___ because it makes its own light.

why.en: Luminous = produces its own light.
why.zh: 发光的 = 自己发光。

items.textzh: 太阳是 ___ 的，因为它自己发光。

items.textzh: 月亮是 ___ 的：我们看到它是因为它反射太阳光。

items.textzh: 在平面镜里，你写的字看起来是反的。这个像是左右 ___ 的。

items.text: The angle of incidence and the angle of reflection are both measured from the ___.

why.en: Always measure from the normal, the 90° line.
why.zh: 总是从法线（90° 的线）开始量。

items.textzh: 入射角和反射角都是从 ___ 量起的。

why.en: Its speed changes, so its direction changes.
why.zh: 速度改变，所以方向改变。

items.textzh: 光从空气进入水中时会弯折。这叫 ___。

items.text: A prism splits white light into colours. This is called ___.

why.zh: 色散 = 白光分成各种颜色。

items.textzh: 棱镜把白光分成各种颜色。这叫 ___。

items.text: A black T-shirt gets hot in the sun because it ___ all the colours of light.

why.zh: 黑色把所有光能吸进去。

items.textzh: 黑 T 恤在太阳下会变热，因为它 ___ 了所有颜色的光。

items.text: Remote controls and thermal cameras use ___.

why.en: Infrared is linked to heat.
why.zh: 红外线和热有关。

items.textzh: 遥控器和热成像相机用的是 ___。

items.text: ___ radiation has enough energy to remove electrons from atoms.

why.zh: 电离辐射可能伤害细胞和 DNA。

items.textzh: ___ 辐射的能量大到能把电子从原子里打出来。

intro.en: 10 questions, 20 seconds each. Faster answers win more points!
intro.zh: 10 道题，每题 20 秒。答得越快分越高！

questions.q: Which wave vibrates at 90° to the way it travels?

why.en: "Transverse" means across. In a transverse wave the particles vibrate at 90° (up and down) to the direction the wave travels, like a Mexican wave or ripples on water.
why.zh: transverse 是“横向”。横波的粒子振动方向和波的传播方向成 90°（上下），像人浪或水波。

longitudinal wave.en: In a longitudinal wave, particles vibrate ALONG (parallel to) the direction of travel, not at 90°.
longitudinal wave.zh: 纵波的粒子是沿着（平行于）传播方向振动，不是 90°。

sound wave.en: Sound is LONGITUDINAL: its particles move back and forth along the direction of travel.
sound wave.zh: 声波是纵波：粒子沿传播方向前后振动。

echo.en: An echo is a reflected sound, so it is also longitudinal.
echo.zh: 回声是反射的声音，所以也是纵波。

questions.qzh: 哪种波的振动方向和传播方向成 90°？

questions.q: Sound is a...

why.en: In sound, the particles vibrate backwards and forwards ALONG the direction the wave travels (compressions and rarefactions). Vibrations parallel to the direction of travel make a longitudinal wave.
why.zh: 声音里，粒子沿着波传播的方向前后振动（疏部和密部）。振动方向和传播方向平行的是纵波。

transverse wave.en: In a transverse wave (light, water ripples), particles move UP and DOWN, at right angles to the direction of travel. Sound particles move back and forth along it.
transverse wave.zh: 横波（光、水波）的粒子上下振动，和传播方向垂直。声音的粒子是沿着方向前后振动。

electromagnetic wave.en: Electromagnetic waves (light, radio) can travel through a vacuum. Sound cannot, because it needs particles.
electromagnetic wave.zh: 电磁波（光、无线电）能在真空中传播。声音不能，因为它需要粒子。

light ray.en: Light is transverse and electromagnetic. Sound is a vibration of particles.
light ray.zh: 光是横波、电磁波。声音是粒子的振动。

questions.qzh: 声音是一种……

questions.q: A louder sound has a bigger...

why.en: Loudness depends ONLY on amplitude: a bigger vibration carries more energy, so the wave is taller and the sound is louder.
why.zh: 响度只取决于振幅：振动越大，能量越多，波越高，声音越响。

frequency.en: Frequency changes PITCH (high or low), not loudness.
frequency.zh: 频率改变的是音调，不是响度。

wavelength.en: Wavelength is linked to pitch, not loudness.
wavelength.zh: 波长和音调有关，和响度无关。

pitch.en: Pitch is how high or low a note is. A quiet note can be high.
pitch.zh: 音调是声音的高低。很小声的音也可以很高。

questions.qzh: 声音越响，……越大。

questions.q: A higher pitch means a higher...

why.en: Pitch depends ONLY on frequency: more vibrations every second = a higher note.
why.zh: 音调只取决于频率：每秒振动次数越多，音越高。

amplitude.zh: 振幅改变的是响度，不是音调。

medium.en: The medium changes the SPEED of sound, not pitch.
medium.zh: 介质改变的是声速，不是音调。

questions.qzh: 音调越高，……越高。

questions.q: A dog whistle at 30,000 Hz is...

why.en: Humans hear about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. 30,000 Hz is ABOVE that, and sound above our hearing is ultrasound (ultra = beyond).
why.zh: 人能听到约 20 Hz 到 20,000 Hz。30,000 Hz 高于这个范围，高于人类听力的是超声波（ultra = 超过）。

infrasound.en: Infrasound is BELOW 20 Hz. 30,000 Hz is very high.
infrasound.zh: 次声波低于 20 Hz。30,000 Hz 非常高。

audible to humans.en: Humans hear only up to about 20,000 Hz. That is why dogs hear the whistle and we don't.
audible to humans.zh: 人只能听到约 20,000 Hz。所以狗听得到哨子，我们听不到。

an echo.en: An echo is a reflected sound, at any frequency. The question is about how high it is.
an echo.zh: 回声是反射的声音，什么频率都可能。题目问的是有多高。

questions.qzh: 30,000 Hz 的狗哨是……

questions.q: Elephants talk with sounds below 20 Hz. This is...

why.en: Sound BELOW 20 Hz, too low for humans to hear, is infrasound (infra = below).
why.zh: 低于 20 Hz、人听不到的声音是次声波（infra = 低于）。

ultrasound.en: Ultrasound is ABOVE 20,000 Hz, very high, the opposite.
ultrasound.zh: 超声波高于 20,000 Hz，很高，正相反。

a decibel.en: A decibel is a unit of LOUDNESS, not a kind of sound.
a decibel.zh: 分贝是响度的单位，不是一种声音。

an echo.en: An echo is a reflected sound, not a frequency range.
an echo.zh: 回声是反射的声音，不是频率范围。

questions.qzh: 大象用低于 20 Hz 的声音交流。这是……

questions.q: Ships find the sea floor using...

why.en: Sonar sends a pulse of sound down and times the ECHO. Sound travels well in water, so distance = speed × time ÷ 2 gives the depth.
why.zh: 声呐向下发出声音脉冲，再测回声的时间。声音在水中传得很好，距离 = 速度 × 时间 ÷ 2，就能算出深度。

x-rays.en: X-rays are used to see inside bodies. They do not travel far through seawater.
x-rays.zh: X 光用来看身体内部，在海水里传不远。

a prism.en: A prism splits light into colours. It cannot measure depth.
a prism.zh: 棱镜把光分成各种颜色，不能测深度。

infrared.en: Infrared is heat radiation. It is absorbed quickly by water.
infrared.zh: 红外线是热辐射，很快就被水吸收了。

questions.qzh: 船用……找到海底。

questions.q: Which part of the ear turns vibrations into electrical signals?

why.en: Cochlea: the spiral in the inner ear.
why.zh: 耳蜗：内耳里的螺旋。

pinna.en: The pinna is the outer ear flap. It only collects sound.
pinna.zh: 耳廓是外耳，只负责收集声音。

eardrum.en: The eardrum VIBRATES when sound hits it, but it does not make electrical signals.
eardrum.zh: 鼓膜被声音打到会振动，但不会产生电信号。

auditory canal.en: The auditory canal is the tube that carries sound to the eardrum.
auditory canal.zh: 耳道是把声音传到鼓膜的管子。

questions.qzh: 耳朵的哪个部分把振动变成电信号？

questions.q: Which material lets NO light through?

why.en: Opaque materials (wood, metal, your hand) block ALL light: none passes through, so they make a sharp shadow.
why.zh: 不透明的材料（木头、金属、手）挡住所有光，一点光都不透，所以会形成清楚的影子。

transparent.en: Transparent materials (clear glass) let almost ALL light through, so you can see clearly through them.
transparent.zh: 透明材料（透明玻璃）几乎让所有光通过，可以清楚地看过去。

translucent.en: Translucent materials (tracing paper) let SOME light through, scattered, so you see only blurry shapes.
translucent.zh: 半透明材料（描图纸）让部分光通过并散开，只能看到模糊的影子。

luminous.en: Luminous means it MAKES its own light (the Sun, a flame). It is not about letting light through.
luminous.zh: 发光是指自己会发光（太阳、火焰），跟让光透过无关。

questions.qzh: 哪种材料一点光都不让通过？

questions.q: Which of these is luminous?

why.en: A flame makes its own light. The Moon only reflects light.
why.zh: 火焰自己发光，月亮只反射光。

the Moon.en: The Moon makes no light of its own. We see it because it REFLECTS sunlight, so it is non-luminous.
the Moon.zh: 月亮自己不发光，我们看到它是因为它反射阳光，所以它不是光源。

a mirror.en: A mirror only reflects light from something else. In the dark it shows nothing.
a mirror.zh: 镜子只是反射别的东西的光，黑暗里什么也照不出来。

a book.en: A book is seen by reflected light. It makes no light itself.
a book.zh: 书是靠反射光被看到的，自己不发光。

questions.qzh: 下面哪个会自己发光？

questions.q: The normal is drawn at...

why.en: Normal = a line at 90° to the surface.
why.zh: 法线 = 和表面成 90° 的线。

45° to the surface.en: 45° is halfway. The normal is always at a RIGHT angle (90°) to the surface.
45° to the surface.zh: 45° 只是一半。法线总是和表面成直角（90°）。

along the surface.en: A line along the surface is at 0°. The normal stands straight up from it.
along the surface.zh: 沿着表面的线是 0°。法线是从表面垂直竖起来的。

180° to the surface.en: 180° is a straight line, which would lie flat along the surface again.
180° to the surface.zh: 180° 是一条直线，又躺回表面上了。

questions.qzh: 法线画在……

questions.q: The three primary colours of light are...

why.en: For LIGHT: red, green, blue. (Red, yellow, blue is for paint.)
why.zh: 光的三原色：红、绿、蓝。（红、黄、蓝是颜料的。）

red, yellow, blue.en: Red, yellow and blue are the primary colours for PAINT, which works by absorbing light. For light we add colours, and the primaries are red, green and blue.
red, yellow, blue.zh: 红、黄、蓝是颜料的三原色，颜料是靠吸收光。光是靠相加，三原色是红、绿、蓝。

cyan, magenta, yellow.en: These are the SECONDARY colours of light (and the ink colours in printers).
cyan, magenta, yellow.zh: 这些是光的二次色（也是打印机墨水的颜色）。

red, orange, yellow.en: Orange can be made by mixing other colours, so it is not a primary colour.
red, orange, yellow.zh: 橙色可以由其他颜色混合出来，所以不是原色。

questions.qzh: 光的三原色是……

questions.q: Red light + green light = ?

why.en: Adding coloured LIGHT: red + green = yellow, red + blue = magenta, green + blue = cyan, and all three = white.
why.zh: 光的颜色相加：红 + 绿 = 黄，红 + 蓝 = 品红，绿 + 蓝 = 青，三种都加 = 白。

white.en: White needs all THREE primaries: red + green + blue.
white.zh: 白光要三种原色都有：红 + 绿 + 蓝。

questions.qzh: 红光 + 绿光 = ？

questions.q: Which EM wave is used to cook food?

why.en: Microwaves: cooking, radar and satellites.
why.zh: 微波：烹饪、雷达和卫星。

radio wave.en: Radio waves carry TV and radio signals. They do not heat food.
radio wave.zh: 无线电波传送电视和广播信号，不会加热食物。

gamma ray.en: Gamma rays are very high energy and dangerous; they are used to kill cancer cells and sterilise equipment.
gamma ray.zh: 伽马射线能量很高很危险，用来杀死癌细胞和消毒器材。

ultraviolet.en: Ultraviolet causes sunburn and is used in security marks, not ovens.
ultraviolet.zh: 紫外线会造成晒伤，用于防伪标记，不是用来做饭。

questions.qzh: 哪种电磁波用来做饭？

questions.q: Which EM wave causes sunburn?

why.en: UV has a higher frequency than visible light and damages skin cells.
why.zh: 紫外线频率比可见光高，会伤害皮肤细胞。

infrared.en: Infrared is felt as HEAT (warmth from a fire). It is lower energy than visible light and does not burn skin cells like UV.
infrared.zh: 红外线让人感到热（火的温暖），能量比可见光低，不会像紫外线那样伤害皮肤细胞。

radio wave.en: Radio waves have very low energy and pass through us harmlessly.
radio wave.zh: 无线电波能量很低，穿过我们的身体也没有害处。

visible light.en: Visible light lets us see. Sunburn comes from the UV just beyond violet.
visible light.zh: 可见光让我们看见东西。晒伤来自紫光外面的紫外线。

questions.qzh: 哪种电磁波会造成晒伤？

questions.q: Which EM waves can travel through a vacuum?

why.en: All EM waves are transverse and need no medium.
why.zh: 所有电磁波都是横波，不需要介质。

only light.en: Light is just one EM wave. All of them, radio to gamma, cross the vacuum of space.
only light.zh: 光只是一种电磁波。从无线电波到伽马射线，全部都能穿过太空真空。

only radio waves.en: Radio waves can, but so can every other EM wave. They do not need particles.
only radio waves.zh: 无线电波可以，其他所有电磁波也可以，它们不需要粒子。

none of them.en: Sunlight reaches us across empty space, so at least light can, and in fact all EM waves can.
none of them.zh: 阳光穿过真空照到我们，所以至少光可以，事实上所有电磁波都可以。

questions.qzh: 哪些电磁波能在真空中传播？

canNow.zh: 我现在能很快地用这些关键词！
