title.zh: 星期四作业：波和声音关键词

subtitle.en: 15 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Study the keyword cards first. Then answer every question. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先学关键词卡片，再回答每道题。可以做很多次。

questions.q: A wave transfers...

why.en: A wave carries ENERGY from one place to another, but the particles only vibrate and stay where they are. (A duck on a wave bobs up and down; it does not travel with the wave.)
why.zh: 波把能量从一个地方传到另一个地方，但粒子只是振动，留在原地。（水面上的鸭子只是上下浮动，不会跟着波走。）

particles.en: The particles only vibrate about one spot. They do not travel along with the wave.
particles.zh: 粒子只在一个位置附近振动，不会跟着波一起走。

water.en: In a water wave the water moves up and down, but it does not travel across the ocean. Energy does.
water.zh: 水波里的水只是上下动，不会横穿大海。传过去的是能量。

air.en: In sound, air particles vibrate back and forth but stay in place. Only the energy moves along.
air.zh: 声音里的空气粒子前后振动但留在原地，只有能量往前传。

questions.qzh: 波传递的是……

questions.q: In a transverse wave, vibrations are ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Perpendicular means at 90° (a right angle). In a transverse wave the particles move up and down while the wave travels forward.
why.zh: perpendicular 是“垂直的”（90°）。横波的粒子上下振动，而波往前传。

parallel.en: Parallel (same direction) describes a LONGITUDINAL wave.

opposite.en: Opposite would be backwards along the line, which is still parallel, not at 90°.
opposite.zh: 相反是沿着直线往回，还是平行，不是 90°。

questions.qzh: 横波的振动方向和传播方向是 ___ 的。

questions.q: In a longitudinal wave, vibrations are ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Parallel means in the same line. In a longitudinal wave (like sound) particles vibrate backwards and forwards along the same line the wave travels.
why.zh: parallel 是“平行的”，在同一条线上。纵波（比如声音）的粒子沿着波传播的同一条线前后振动。

at 45°.en: Neither kind of wave vibrates at 45°. It is either parallel (longitudinal) or 90° (transverse).
at 45°.zh: 两种波都不是 45° 振动，要么平行（纵波），要么 90°（横波）。

random.en: The vibrations follow a pattern; they are not random.
random.zh: 振动是有规律的，不是随机的。

questions.qzh: 纵波的振动方向和传播方向是 ___ 的。

questions.q: The distance from one crest to the next crest is the...

why.en: Wavelength is the length of ONE complete wave: from a point on one wave to the same point on the next, like crest to crest.
why.zh: 波长是一个完整的波的长度：从一个波上的某点到下一个波的同一点，比如波峰到波峰。

amplitude.en: Amplitude is the HEIGHT from the middle line to a crest, not a length along the wave.
amplitude.zh: 振幅是从中线到波峰的高度，不是沿着波的长度。

frequency.en: Frequency is how many waves pass each SECOND. It is a number per second, not a distance.
frequency.zh: 频率是每秒经过多少个波，是每秒的数量，不是距离。

pitch.en: Pitch is how high or low a sound is, which depends on frequency.
pitch.zh: 音调是声音的高低，取决于频率。

questions.qzh: 从一个波峰到下一个波峰的距离是……

questions.q: The maximum distance a point moves from its resting position is the...

why.en: That is the exact meaning of amplitude.
why.zh: 这就是振幅的意思。

wavelength.en: Wavelength is the length of one whole wave (crest to crest), along the wave.
wavelength.zh: 波长是一个完整波的长度（波峰到波峰），是沿着波的。

frequency.en: Frequency is waves per second, not a distance.
frequency.zh: 频率是每秒的波数，不是距离。

medium.en: The medium is the material the wave travels through (air, water).
medium.zh: 介质是波传播经过的物质（空气、水）。

questions.qzh: 一个点离开平衡位置的最大距离是……

questions.q: 5 complete waves pass a point every second. The frequency is...

why.en: Frequency = waves per second. 5 per second = 5 Hz.
why.zh: 频率 = 每秒的波数。每秒 5 个 = 5 Hz。

1/5 Hz.en: 1/5 Hz would be one wave every 5 seconds. Here 5 waves pass EVERY second.
1/5 Hz.zh: 1/5 Hz 是 5 秒一个波。这里是每秒 5 个波。

5 dB.en: Decibels measure LOUDNESS, not frequency. Frequency is in hertz (Hz).
5 dB.zh: 分贝测的是响度，不是频率。频率的单位是赫兹（Hz）。

50 Hz.en: 50 Hz would be 50 waves every second. There are only 5.
50 Hz.zh: 50 Hz 是每秒 50 个波。这里只有 5 个。

questions.qzh: 每秒有 5 个完整的波经过一个点。频率是……

questions.q: A space containing no particles is a...

why.en: No particles = vacuum. Sound cannot travel there.
why.zh: 没有粒子 = 真空，声音不能在那里传播。

medium.en: A medium is the OPPOSITE: a material full of particles that a wave travels through.
medium.zh: 介质正相反：是充满粒子、让波通过的物质。

compression.en: A compression is where particles are squashed CLOSE together, the opposite of empty.
compression.zh: 密部是粒子挤在一起的地方，和“空”正相反。

spectrum.en: A spectrum is a range of waves or colours, like the rainbow.
spectrum.zh: 光谱是一系列波或颜色，比如彩虹。

questions.qzh: 没有任何粒子的空间叫……

questions.q: In a longitudinal wave, where particles are spread further apart is a...

why.en: Spread apart = rarefaction. Close together = compression.
why.zh: 分开 = 疏部；挤在一起 = 密部。

compression.en: A compression is where particles are squashed CLOSE together.
compression.zh: 密部是粒子挤在一起的地方。

crest.en: Crests belong to TRANSVERSE waves (the top of a wave), not to spreading in a longitudinal wave.
crest.zh: 波峰属于横波（波的最高点），不是纵波里粒子散开的地方。

vacuum.en: A vacuum has NO particles at all. A rarefaction still has particles, just spread out.
vacuum.zh: 真空里一个粒子都没有。疏部还有粒子，只是分散开了。

questions.qzh: 在纵波里，粒子分得比较开的地方叫……

questions.q: Pitch depends on the...

why.en: Pitch depends ONLY on frequency: more vibrations per second = higher note.
why.zh: 音调只取决于频率：每秒振动越多，音越高。

amplitude.zh: 振幅改变响度，不是音调。

decibels.zh: 分贝测量响度，不是音调。

medium.en: The medium changes how fast sound travels, not its pitch.
medium.zh: 介质改变声速，不是音调。

questions.qzh: 音调取决于……

questions.q: Loudness is related to the...

why.en: Loudness depends ONLY on amplitude: bigger vibrations carry more energy and sound louder.
why.zh: 响度只取决于振幅：振动越大，能量越多，声音越响。

frequency.zh: 频率改变音调，不是响度。

wavelength.en: Wavelength is linked to pitch, not loudness.
wavelength.zh: 波长和音调有关，不是响度。

pitch.en: Pitch is high or low, not loud or quiet.
pitch.zh: 音调是高低，不是大小声。

questions.qzh: 响度和……有关。

questions.q: The human audible range is about...

why.en: Humans can hear sounds from about 20 Hz (a very low rumble) to about 20,000 Hz (a very high whistle).
why.zh: 人能听到约 20 Hz（很低的隆隆声）到约 20,000 Hz（很高的哨声）的声音。

0 Hz to 100 Hz.en: This is far too low and too narrow. We hear up to about 20,000 Hz.
0 Hz to 100 Hz.zh: 这太低也太窄了。我们能听到约 20,000 Hz。

20 dB to 200 dB.en: dB measures LOUDNESS. The audible range is about frequency, in Hz.
20 dB to 200 dB.zh: dB 测的是响度。可听范围讲的是频率，用 Hz。

200 Hz to 2,000 Hz.en: This range is too narrow. It misses the lowest and highest sounds we hear.
200 Hz to 2,000 Hz.zh: 这个范围太窄，漏掉了我们能听到的最低和最高的声音。

questions.qzh: 人能听到的范围大约是……

questions.q: Sound heard again after reflecting off a surface is an...

why.en: An echo is a sound you hear again because it REFLECTED (bounced) off a hard surface, like a cliff or a wall.
why.zh: 回声是声音碰到坚硬的表面（悬崖、墙）反射回来，你又听到一次。

ultrasound.en: Ultrasound is sound above 20,000 Hz. It is about frequency, not reflection.
ultrasound.zh: 超声波是高于 20,000 Hz 的声音，讲的是频率，不是反射。

eardrum.en: The eardrum is part of the ear, not a sound.
eardrum.zh: 鼓膜是耳朵的一部分，不是声音。

infrasound.en: Infrasound is sound below 20 Hz, not reflected sound.
infrasound.zh: 次声波是低于 20 Hz 的声音，不是反射的声音。

questions.qzh: 声音碰到表面反射回来又被听到，叫……

questions.q: Which part collects sound waves on the outside of the ear?

why.en: Pinna: the visible outer part of the ear.
why.zh: 耳廓：耳朵外面看得见的部分。

cochlea.en: The cochlea is deep in the INNER ear. It turns vibrations into signals.
cochlea.zh: 耳蜗在内耳深处，把振动变成信号。

ossicles.en: The ossicles are tiny bones in the MIDDLE ear that pass the vibration on.
ossicles.zh: 听小骨是中耳里的小骨头，负责传递振动。

auditory nerve.en: The auditory nerve carries signals to the brain, deep inside the head.
auditory nerve.zh: 听神经在头部深处，把信号送到大脑。

questions.qzh: 耳朵外面收集声波的部分是……

questions.q: Put the ear in order: pinna → auditory canal → ___ → ossicles → cochlea → auditory nerve

why.en: At the end of the auditory canal, sound hits the EARDRUM, a thin skin that vibrates and passes the vibration to the ossicles.
why.zh: 声音走到耳道尽头会打到鼓膜，一层薄膜会振动，把振动传给听小骨。

brain.en: The brain is at the very end, after the auditory nerve.
brain.zh: 大脑在最后，在听神经之后。

sonar.en: Sonar is a technology using echoes, not part of the ear.
sonar.zh: 声呐是利用回声的技术，不是耳朵的一部分。

pinna.en: The pinna is the FIRST part, already at the start of the list.
pinna.zh: 耳廓是第一部分，已经在开头了。

questions.qzh: 给耳朵排顺序：耳廓 → 耳道 → ___ → 听小骨 → 耳蜗 → 听神经

questions.q: What carries electrical signals from the cochlea to the brain?

why.en: Nerve = carries signals to the brain.
why.zh: 神经 = 把信号送到大脑。

auditory canal.en: The auditory canal carries SOUND to the eardrum, not electrical signals to the brain.
auditory canal.zh: 耳道把声音送到鼓膜，不是把电信号送到大脑。

eardrum.en: The eardrum vibrates. It does not carry signals to the brain.
eardrum.zh: 鼓膜只会振动，不会把信号送到大脑。

pinna.en: The pinna collects sound on the outside.

questions.qzh: 什么把电信号从耳蜗送到大脑？

canNow.en: I can now answer keyword questions by myself.
canNow.zh: 我现在能自己回答关键词的问题。

title.en: Friday Homework: Light and EM Keywords
title.zh: 星期五作业：光和电磁波关键词

subtitle.en: 15 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Read Main Book B4 to B8 and study the cards first. Then answer every question. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 B4 到 B8，学卡片，再回答每道题。可以做很多次。

questions.q: A material that lets light pass through clearly is...

why.en: Clearly through = transparent (like window glass).
why.zh: 能看清 = 透明（像窗玻璃）。

translucent.en: Translucent lets SOME light through but scatters it, so you cannot see clearly (like frosted glass).
translucent.zh: 半透明让部分光通过但会散开，所以看不清（像磨砂玻璃）。

opaque.zh: 不透明一点光都不让通过。

luminous.en: Luminous means it makes its own light, not that light passes through it.
luminous.zh: 发光是自己会发光，不是光能穿过。

questions.qzh: 能让光清楚地穿过的材料是……

questions.q: Tracing paper lets light through, but you cannot see clearly through it. It is...

why.en: Light gets through but scatters: translucent.
why.zh: 光能通过但会散开：半透明。

transparent.en: Transparent means you CAN see clearly through it, like clear glass. Tracing paper is blurry.
transparent.zh: 透明是能清楚地看过去，像透明玻璃。描图纸是模糊的。

opaque.en: Opaque lets NO light through, but tracing paper lets some through.
opaque.zh: 不透明一点光都不透，但描图纸会透一些光。

non-luminous.en: Non-luminous only means it makes no light. That is true but does not describe how light passes through.
non-luminous.zh: 不发光只是说它自己不发光，这没错，但没有说明光怎样穿过它。

questions.qzh: 描图纸能透光，但看不清楚后面的东西。它是……

questions.q: Which is NON-luminous?

why.en: The Moon does not make light. We see it by reflected sunlight.
why.zh: 月亮不发光，我们看到的是它反射的太阳光。

the Sun.en: The Sun MAKES its own light, so it is luminous.

a torch that is on.en: A torch that is on makes its own light: luminous.
a torch that is on.zh: 开着的手电筒自己发光：是光源。

a candle flame.en: A flame makes its own light: luminous.

questions.qzh: 哪个不会自己发光？

questions.q: The angle between the incident ray and the normal is the...

why.en: Incident ray + normal = angle of incidence.
why.zh: 入射光线和法线 = 入射角。

angle of reflection.en: The angle of reflection is between the REFLECTED ray and the normal.
angle of reflection.zh: 反射角是反射光线和法线之间的角。

right angle.en: A right angle is the 90° between the normal and the mirror, not the angle of the ray.
right angle.zh: 直角是法线和镜面之间的 90°，不是光线的角。

angle of refraction.en: Refraction is light BENDING into a new material. Its angle is between the refracted ray and the normal.
angle of refraction.zh: 折射是光进入新物质时弯折，折射角是折射光线和法线之间的角。

questions.qzh: 入射光线和法线之间的角叫……

questions.q: The angle of incidence is 35°. The angle of reflection is...

why.en: Law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
why.zh: 反射定律：入射角 = 反射角。

55°.en: 55° is 90° − 35°, the angle from the MIRROR surface. Both angles are measured from the normal, so they are equal.
55°.zh: 55° 是 90° − 35°，是从镜面量的角。两个角都从法线量，所以相等。

90°.en: 90° is the angle between the normal and the mirror, not the reflection angle.
90°.zh: 90° 是法线和镜面之间的角，不是反射角。

145°.en: 145° is 180° − 35°. The law of reflection says the two angles are EQUAL.
145°.zh: 145° 是 180° − 35°。反射定律说两个角相等。

questions.qzh: 入射角是 35°。反射角是……

questions.q: Light bends when it goes from air into glass because its ___ changes.

why.en: Refraction: direction changes because the speed changes.
why.zh: 折射：速度改变，所以方向改变。

colour.en: The colour of the light stays the same when it enters glass.
colour.zh: 光进入玻璃时颜色不变。

amplitude.en: Amplitude is about brightness, and changing it does not bend light.
amplitude.zh: 振幅关系到亮度，改变它不会让光弯折。

brightness.en: Brightness has nothing to do with bending. The change in SPEED causes refraction.
brightness.zh: 亮度和弯折无关，是速度的变化造成折射。

questions.qzh: 光从空气进入玻璃时会弯折，因为它的 ___ 变了。

questions.q: White light splitting into colours is called...

why.en: Dispersion = separating white light into its colours.
why.zh: 色散 = 白光分成各种颜色。

reflection.en: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface. It does not split the colours.
reflection.zh: 反射是光从表面反弹回来，不会把颜色分开。

absorption.en: Absorption is when a material takes in light. It removes colours rather than spreading them out.
absorption.zh: 吸收是物质把光吸进去，是去掉颜色，不是把颜色分开。

inversion.en: Inversion means turning upside down (like an image in a pinhole camera).
inversion.zh: 倒置是上下颠倒（像针孔相机里的像）。

questions.qzh: 白光分成各种颜色叫……

questions.q: The secondary colours of light are...

why.en: Adding two primary colours of LIGHT gives a secondary colour: red + green = yellow, red + blue = magenta, green + blue = cyan.
why.zh: 两种光的原色相加得到二次色：红 + 绿 = 黄，红 + 蓝 = 品红，绿 + 蓝 = 青。

red, green, blue.en: These are the PRIMARY colours of light, the ones you start with.
red, green, blue.zh: 这些是光的三原色，是起点。

red, yellow, blue.en: These are the primary colours of PAINT, not the secondary colours of light.
red, yellow, blue.zh: 这些是颜料的三原色，不是光的二次色。

orange, green, purple.en: These are the secondary colours of PAINT. Light mixes differently because it adds instead of absorbing.
orange, green, purple.zh: 这些是颜料的二次色。光是相加而不是吸收，所以混合方式不同。

questions.qzh: 光的二次色是……

questions.q: A red apple looks red because it...
options: reflects red light and absorbs the other colours

why.en: We see the colour that is reflected into our eyes.
why.zh: 我们看到的是反射进眼睛的颜色。

absorbs red light.en: If it absorbed red, no red would reach your eyes. We see the colour that is REFLECTED.
absorbs red light.zh: 如果它吸收了红光，就没有红光进入眼睛。我们看到的是被反射的颜色。

makes its own red light.en: An apple is non-luminous; it makes no light. It reflects light from the Sun or a lamp.
makes its own red light.zh: 苹果不发光，它反射太阳或灯的光。

transmits all colours.en: Transmitting all colours means light goes straight through, so it would look clear like glass.
transmits all colours.zh: 让所有颜色通过就是光直接穿过去，它会像玻璃一样透明。

questions.qzh: 红苹果看起来是红色的，因为它……

ozh.reflects red light and absorbs the other: 反射红光，吸收其他颜色

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves are...
options: transverse, and can travel through a vacuum

why.en: EM wave: a transverse wave that can travel through a vacuum.
why.zh: 电磁波：能在真空中传播的横波。

longitudinal, and need a medium.en: That describes SOUND. EM waves are transverse and need no particles, which is how sunlight crosses space.
longitudinal, and need a medium.zh: 那是声波。电磁波是横波，不需要粒子，所以阳光能穿过太空。

sound waves.en: Sound is a vibration of particles. EM waves are a different family that can cross a vacuum.
sound waves.zh: 声音是粒子的振动。电磁波是另一类，能穿过真空。

only visible light.en: Visible light is only a small part of the EM spectrum: radio, microwave, infrared, UV, X-ray and gamma are EM waves too.
only visible light.zh: 可见光只是电磁波谱的一小部分：无线电波、微波、红外线、紫外线、X 光和伽马射线都是电磁波。

questions.qzh: 电磁波是……

questions.q: Which EM wave has the LOWEST frequency?

why.en: EM spectrum from lowest to highest frequency: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-ray, Gamma. Radio waves are at the LOW end (and have the longest wavelength).
why.zh: 电磁波谱从低频到高频：无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 光、伽马射线。无线电波在低频端（波长最长）。

gamma ray.en: Gamma rays are at the HIGHEST frequency end.
gamma ray.zh: 伽马射线在最高频的一端。

x-ray.en: X-rays are very high frequency, second only to gamma.
x-ray.zh: X 光频率很高，仅次于伽马射线。

ultraviolet.en: Ultraviolet is higher than visible light, near the top end.
ultraviolet.zh: 紫外线比可见光高，接近高频端。

questions.qzh: 哪种电磁波的频率最低？

questions.q: Which EM wave is used in thermal imaging and remote controls?

why.en: Infrared is linked to heat.
why.zh: 红外线和热有关。

microwave.en: Microwaves are used for cooking, radar and phone signals.
microwave.zh: 微波用于做饭、雷达和手机信号。

x-ray.en: X-rays are for seeing bones inside the body.
x-ray.zh: X 光用来看身体里的骨头。

gamma ray.en: Gamma rays are for cancer treatment and sterilising.
gamma ray.zh: 伽马射线用于治疗癌症和消毒。

questions.qzh: 热成像和遥控器用的是哪种电磁波？

questions.q: X-rays are used for medical images because they...

why.en: X-rays pass through soft tissue but not bone.
why.zh: X 射线能穿过软组织，但穿不过骨头。

questions.qzh: X 光用于医学影像，因为它们……

questions.q: Which EM wave is used in cancer treatment?

why.en: Gamma rays: very high-frequency, used in cancer treatment.
why.zh: 伽马射线：频率非常高，用于治疗癌症。

radio wave.en: Radio waves have very low energy, far too low to kill cancer cells.
radio wave.zh: 无线电波能量很低，远不足以杀死癌细胞。

infrared.en: Infrared is heat radiation, used in remote controls and thermal cameras.
infrared.zh: 红外线是热辐射，用于遥控器和热成像。

visible light.en: Visible light lets us see. It does not have enough energy to destroy cancer cells.
visible light.zh: 可见光让我们看见东西，能量不够摧毁癌细胞。

questions.qzh: 治疗癌症用的是哪种电磁波？

questions.q: Ionising radiation is dangerous because it can...

why.en: It has enough energy to remove electrons from atoms.
why.zh: 它的能量大到能把电子从原子中打出来。

make things invisible.en: No EM wave makes things invisible. The danger is the energy hitting living cells.
make things invisible.zh: 没有电磁波能让东西隐形。危险在于能量打在活细胞上。

stop sound.en: EM waves and sound are separate; radiation does not stop sound.
stop sound.zh: 电磁波和声音是两回事，辐射不会让声音停止。

cool things down.en: Absorbed radiation adds energy, which HEATS things, not cools them. The real danger is damage to cells.
cool things down.zh: 被吸收的辐射会增加能量，让东西变热，不是变冷。真正的危险是伤害细胞。

questions.qzh: 电离辐射很危险，因为它会……

canNow.en: I can now answer keyword questions by myself.
canNow.zh: 我现在能自己回答关键词的问题。

title.en: B4 and B5 Quiz: Light and Reflection
title.zh: B4 和 B5 小测：光和反射

intro.en: The big rule: angle of incidence = angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.
intro.zh: 最重要的规则：入射角 = 反射角，都从法线量起。

questions.q: Window glass is...

why.en: Light passes clearly: transparent.
why.zh: 光清楚地通过：透明。

translucent.en: Translucent glass (frosted) is blurry. You can see clearly through a window, so it is transparent.
translucent.zh: 半透明玻璃（磨砂）看不清。窗户能看清楚，所以是透明的。

opaque.en: Opaque blocks all light. Light comes through a window.
opaque.zh: 不透明会挡住所有光。窗户是透光的。

luminous.en: Luminous means it makes its own light. Glass does not.
luminous.zh: 发光是自己发光，玻璃不会。

questions.qzh: 窗户玻璃是……

questions.q: Frosted bathroom glass is...

why.en: Light passes but scatters: translucent.
why.zh: 光能通过但会散开：半透明。

transparent.en: Transparent means you can see clearly through it. Frosted glass is blurry on purpose.
transparent.zh: 透明是能清楚看过去。磨砂玻璃故意做成模糊的。

opaque.en: Opaque blocks ALL light, but frosted glass still lets light into the bathroom.
opaque.zh: 不透明会挡住所有光，但磨砂玻璃还是让光进到浴室。

non-luminous only.en: It is non-luminous, but that only says it makes no light. The question is how light passes through.
non-luminous only.zh: 它确实不发光，但那只说明它自己不发光。题目问的是光怎样穿过。

questions.qzh: 浴室的磨砂玻璃是……

questions.q: A wooden door is...

why.en: No light passes: opaque.
why.zh: 光不能通过：不透明。

transparent.en: You cannot see through a wooden door, so it is not transparent.
transparent.zh: 木门看不过去，所以不透明。

translucent.en: Translucent lets some light through. A wooden door lets none.
translucent.zh: 半透明会透一些光。木门一点都不透。

luminous.en: A door makes no light of its own.

questions.qzh: 木门是……

questions.q: Which is LUMINOUS?

why.en: It makes its own light.
why.zh: 它自己发光。

the Moon.en: The Moon only REFLECTS sunlight, so it is non-luminous.
the Moon.zh: 月亮只是反射阳光，所以不是光源。

a mirror.en: A mirror only reflects light from other things.
a mirror.zh: 镜子只反射别的东西的光。

a white wall.en: A white wall reflects a lot of light but makes none itself.
a white wall.zh: 白墙反射很多光，但自己不发光。

questions.qzh: 哪个会自己发光？

questions.q: We see a book because...
options: light reflects off it into our eyes

why.en: Non-luminous objects are seen by reflected light.
why.zh: 不发光的物体靠反射光被看见。

it makes its own light.en: A book is non-luminous: in a dark room you cannot see it.
it makes its own light.zh: 书不发光：在黑屋子里你看不到它。

our eyes send out light.en: Eyes RECEIVE light; they do not send it out. That is why we cannot see in the dark.
our eyes send out light.zh: 眼睛是接收光，不是发出光。所以在黑暗中看不见。

it is opaque.en: Being opaque only means light cannot pass through it. We see it because light BOUNCES off it into our eyes.
it is opaque.zh: 不透明只表示光穿不过去。我们看到它是因为光从它上面反射进眼睛。

questions.qzh: 我们能看到书，是因为……

ozh.light reflects off it into our eyes: 光从它上面反射进我们的眼睛

questions.q: Light rays are drawn as...

why.en: Light travels in straight lines. The arrow shows the direction.
why.zh: 光沿直线传播，箭头表示方向。

wavy lines.en: Light is a wave, but a ray shows the PATH it travels, which is straight.
wavy lines.zh: 光是波，但光线表示的是它走的路线，是直的。

circles.en: Circles do not show a direction of travel.
circles.zh: 圆圈不能表示传播方向。

dotted curves.en: Light does not curve in air. Dotted lines are only used for the normal or for virtual rays behind a mirror.
dotted curves.zh: 光在空气中不会弯。虚线只用来画法线或镜子后面的虚像光线。

questions.qzh: 光线画成……

questions.q: The angle of incidence is 30°. The angle of reflection is...

why.en: Law of reflection: the angle of incidence EQUALS the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal. 30° in, 30° out.
why.zh: 反射定律：入射角等于反射角，都从法线量。入射 30°，反射也是 30°。

60°.en: 60° is 90° − 30°, the angle from the mirror surface. Angles are measured from the normal, so it stays 30°.
60°.zh: 60° 是 90° − 30°，是从镜面量的。角要从法线量，所以还是 30°。

90°.en: 90° is the angle between the normal and the mirror.
90°.zh: 90° 是法线和镜面之间的角。

150°.en: 150° is 180° − 30°. The law says the two angles are equal.

questions.qzh: 入射角是 30°。反射角是……

questions.q: Angles in a ray diagram are measured from the...

why.en: The normal is a line at 90° to the surface where the ray hits. All angles in ray diagrams are measured from it, so the law of reflection works on any surface.
why.zh: 法线是在光线射到的地方和表面成 90° 的线。光路图里所有角都从它量，这样反射定律在任何表面都适用。

mirror surface.en: Measuring from the mirror gives the wrong angle (90° minus the real one).
mirror surface.zh: 从镜面量会得到错误的角（90° 减去真正的角）。

top of the page.en: The page has nothing to do with the ray; the normal is drawn where the ray hits.
top of the page.zh: 纸的边和光线无关，法线画在光线射到的地方。

light source.en: The light source can be anywhere. Angles are measured at the mirror, from the normal.
light source.zh: 光源可以在任何地方。角是在镜面上从法线量的。

questions.qzh: 光路图里的角是从……量的。

questions.q: The ray that bounces OFF the mirror is the...

why.en: Incident = going in. Reflected = bouncing off.
why.zh: 入射 = 射进来；反射 = 弹出去。

incident ray.en: The incident ray is the one going IN, towards the mirror.
incident ray.zh: 入射光线是射向镜子的那条。

normal.en: The normal is the 90° construction line, not a ray of light.
normal.zh: 法线是画出来的 90° 辅助线，不是光线。

refracted ray.en: A refracted ray goes INTO a new material and bends, like into glass or water.
refracted ray.zh: 折射光线是进入新物质时弯折的光线，比如进入玻璃或水。

questions.qzh: 从镜子上反弹回来的光线叫……

questions.q: In a plane mirror, your right hand looks like a left hand. This is called...

why.en: Laterally inverted = reversed left to right.
why.zh: 左右颠倒 = 左右反过来。

refraction.en: Refraction is light bending as it enters a new material.
refraction.zh: 折射是光进入新物质时弯折。

dispersion.en: Dispersion is white light splitting into colours.
dispersion.zh: 色散是白光分成各种颜色。

absorption.en: Absorption is a material taking in light.
absorption.zh: 吸收是物质把光吸进去。

questions.qzh: 在平面镜里，你的右手看起来像左手。这叫……

canNow.en: I can now sort materials and use the law of reflection.
canNow.zh: 我现在会给材料分类，并会用反射定律。

intro.en: Read the sentence, then tap the missing word.
intro.zh: 读句子，然后点出缺少的词。

items.text: The ___ ray travels towards the mirror.

why.en: Incident = coming in.
why.zh: 入射 = 射进来。

items.textzh: ___ 光线射向镜子。

items.text: The ___ ray bounces off the mirror.

why.en: Reflected = bounced off.
why.zh: 反射 = 弹出去。

items.textzh: ___ 光线从镜子上反弹回来。

items.text: The ___ is a dashed line at 90° to the mirror.

why.en: Draw the normal first.
why.zh: 先画法线。

items.textzh: ___ 是一条和镜子成 90° 的虚线。

items.text: The angle of incidence is ___ to the angle of reflection.

why.en: Law of reflection.
why.zh: 反射定律。

items.textzh: 入射角 ___ 反射角。

items.text: A flat mirror is called a ___ mirror.

why.en: Plane = flat.
why.zh: plane = 平的。

items.textzh: 平的镜子叫 ___ 镜。

items.text: Mirror writing looks back to front because the image is laterally ___.

why.en: Reversed left to right.
why.zh: 左右反过来。

items.textzh: 镜子里的字看起来是反的，因为像是左右 ___ 的。

items.text: A material that lets light through clearly is ___.

why.en: You can see through it clearly.
why.zh: 可以清楚地看过去。

items.textzh: 让光清楚地穿过的材料是 ___ 的。

items.text: A material that lets NO light through is ___.

why.en: Opaque blocks light and makes shadows.
why.zh: 不透明的物体挡住光，形成影子。

items.textzh: 一点光都不让通过的材料是 ___ 的。

canNow.en: I can now label a ray diagram.
canNow.zh: 我现在会标注光路图。

title.en: Saturday Homework: Chemistry Review (A1 to A8)
title.zh: 星期六作业：化学复习（A1 到 A8）

subtitle.en: 12 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Keep the chemistry fresh! Look at your Main Book if you need to. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 别忘了化学！需要的话看主课本。可以做很多次。

questions.q: Which is a MIXTURE?

why.en: Air is many gases mixed, not joined.
why.zh: 空气是很多气体混在一起，没有结合。

water (H₂O).en: Water has one formula, H₂O: hydrogen and oxygen joined, a compound.
water (H₂O).zh: 水有一个化学式 H₂O：氢和氧结合，是化合物。

oxygen (O₂).en: O₂ has one kind of atom, so it is an element.
oxygen (O₂).zh: O₂ 只有一种原子，是单质。

carbon dioxide (CO₂).en: CO₂ has one formula: carbon and oxygen joined, a compound.
carbon dioxide (CO₂).zh: CO₂ 有一个化学式：碳和氧结合，是化合物。

questions.qzh: 哪个是混合物？

questions.q: Which is an ELEMENT?

why.en: Each CAPITAL letter in a formula is a different element. Mg has only one capital letter, so only one kind of atom: an element (magnesium).
why.zh: 化学式里每个大写字母是一种元素。Mg 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子：单质（镁）。

MgO.en: Two capital letters (Mg, O): magnesium and oxygen joined, a compound.
MgO.zh: 两个大写字母（Mg、O）：镁和氧结合，是化合物。

CO.en: Two capital letters (C, O): carbon monoxide, a compound.
CO.zh: 两个大写字母（C、O）：一氧化碳，是化合物。

NaCl.en: Two capital letters (Na, Cl): a compound.

questions.qzh: 哪个是单质？

questions.q: Which is a COMPOUND?

why.en: A compound has two or more DIFFERENT elements chemically joined. CO₂ has two capital letters (C and O), so it is a compound.
why.zh: 化合物是两种或更多不同元素化学结合。CO₂ 有两个大写字母（C 和 O），所以是化合物。

O₂.en: O₂ is two atoms of the SAME element, so it is an element.
O₂.zh: O₂ 是两个同种原子，是单质。

N₂.en: N₂ is two atoms of the SAME element, so it is an element.
N₂.zh: N₂ 是两个同种原子，是单质。

Cu.en: Cu (copper) has one capital letter: an element.
Cu.zh: Cu（铜）只有一个大写字母：单质。

questions.qzh: 哪个是化合物？

questions.q: How many atoms are in ONE molecule of CH₄?

why.en: Count every atom: C has no number, so 1 carbon; H₄ means 4 hydrogens. 1 + 4 = 5 atoms.
why.zh: 数所有原子：C 没写数字，就是 1 个碳；H₄ 是 4 个氢。1 + 4 = 5 个原子。

4.en: 4 counts only the hydrogens. Don't forget the 1 carbon.
4.zh: 4 只数了氢，别忘了 1 个碳。

2.en: 2 is the number of different ELEMENTS (C and H), not the number of atoms.
2.zh: 2 是元素种类数（C 和 H），不是原子数。

1.en: 1 is the number of molecules, or only the carbon. There are 5 atoms inside it.
1.zh: 1 是分子数，或只数了碳。里面有 5 个原子。

questions.qzh: 一个 CH₄ 分子里有几个原子？

questions.q: How many oxygen atoms are in 2H₂O?

why.en: The big 2 in front means 2 MOLECULES of water. Each H₂O has 1 oxygen (O has no small number, so 1). 2 × 1 = 2 oxygen atoms.
why.zh: 前面大的 2 表示 2 个水分子。每个 H₂O 有 1 个氧（O 没写小数字，就是 1）。2 × 1 = 2 个氧原子。

4.en: 4 is the number of HYDROGEN atoms (2 × 2). The question asks for oxygen.
4.zh: 4 是氢原子数（2 × 2）。题目问的是氧。

1.en: 1 is the oxygen in ONE molecule. There are 2 molecules.
1.zh: 1 是一个分子里的氧，这里有 2 个分子。

6.en: 6 is ALL the atoms (2 × 3). The question asks only for oxygen.
6.zh: 6 是所有原子（2 × 3）。题目只问氧。

questions.qzh: 2H₂O 里有几个氧原子？

questions.q: magnesium + oxygen → ?

why.en: Metal + oxygen → metal OXIDE. Keep the metal name first and change oxygen to oxide. MgO has one oxygen, so no prefix: magnesium oxide.
why.zh: 金属 + 氧 → 金属氧化物。金属名称在前，oxygen 改成 oxide。MgO 只有一个氧，不加前缀：magnesium oxide（氧化镁）。

magnesium oxygenide.zh: oxygen 加 -ide 的形式是 oxide，不是 oxygenide。

magnesium dioxide.en: Di- means 2 oxygens. Magnesium oxide (MgO) has only one.
magnesium dioxide.zh: di- 表示 2 个氧。氧化镁（MgO）只有一个。

oxygen magnesium.en: The metal comes FIRST, and oxygen changes to oxide at the end.
oxygen magnesium.zh: 金属在前，oxygen 在后面改成 oxide。

questions.qzh: 镁 + 氧 → ?（选正确的英文名称）

questions.q: In a word equation, the substances on the LEFT of the arrow are the...

why.en: In a word equation, reactants (what you START with) go on the left, and the arrow points to the products (what is MADE) on the right.
why.zh: 文字方程式里，反应物（开始时有的）写在左边，箭头指向右边的生成物（生成的东西）。

products.en: Products are what is MADE, on the RIGHT of the arrow.
products.zh: 生成物是生成的东西，在箭头右边。

elements.en: The left side can contain elements or compounds. "Reactants" is the name for its position.
elements.zh: 左边可以是单质也可以是化合物。reactants 是这个位置的名称。

mixtures.en: Reactants are substances that react. They are not called mixtures.
mixtures.zh: 反应物是参加反应的物质，不叫混合物。

questions.qzh: 在文字方程式里，箭头左边的物质叫……

questions.q: Which is a CHEMICAL change?

why.en: A chemical change makes a NEW substance and cannot easily be reversed. Burning paper makes ash, smoke and gases, and you cannot turn them back into paper.
why.zh: 化学变化产生新物质，不容易逆转。烧纸会产生灰、烟和气体，没法变回纸。

melting ice.en: Melting is a change of STATE. It is still water and can freeze again: physical.
melting ice.zh: 熔化是状态变化，还是水，可以再冻起来：物理变化。

dissolving sugar.en: The sugar is still there (the water tastes sweet) and you can get it back by evaporating: physical.
dissolving sugar.zh: 糖还在（水是甜的），蒸发后可以拿回来：物理变化。

cutting paper.en: Cut paper is still paper, just smaller pieces: physical.
cutting paper.zh: 剪开的纸还是纸，只是变小了：物理变化。

questions.qzh: 哪个是化学变化？

questions.q: Mass before a reaction = 10 g. Mass after (nothing escapes) = ?

why.en: Conservation of mass: atoms are never made or destroyed in a reaction, only rearranged. If nothing escapes, the mass stays the same: 10 g.
why.zh: 质量守恒：反应中原子不会产生也不会消失，只是重新组合。没有东西跑掉，质量就不变：10 克。

less than 10 g.en: Mass only goes down if something (like a gas) ESCAPES. The question says nothing escapes.
less than 10 g.zh: 只有东西（比如气体）跑掉，质量才会下降。题目说没有东西跑掉。

more than 10 g.en: Mass only goes up if something is ADDED from outside (like oxygen from the air). Nothing was added.
more than 10 g.zh: 只有从外面加进东西（比如空气中的氧），质量才会上升。这里没有加。

0 g.en: The atoms are still all there, just joined differently.
0 g.zh: 原子都还在，只是连接方式变了。

questions.qzh: 反应前质量 = 10 g。反应后（没有东西跑掉）= ？

questions.q: Liquid → solid is called...

why.en: Cooling a liquid until it turns solid: freezing.
why.zh: 液体冷却变成固体：凝固。

melting.en: Melting is the opposite: solid → liquid.
melting.zh: 熔化正相反：固体 → 液体。

questions.qzh: 液体 → 固体叫……

questions.q: A substance melts at -10 °C and boils at 80 °C. At 20 °C it is a...

why.en: 20 is above -10 (melted) and below 80 (not boiled): liquid.
why.zh: 20 高于 -10（已熔化），低于 80（没沸腾）：液体。

solid.en: It would be solid BELOW −10 °C. 20 °C is above its melting point.
solid.zh: 低于 −10 °C 才是固体。20 °C 高于熔点。

gas.en: It would be a gas ABOVE 80 °C. 20 °C is below its boiling point.
gas.zh: 高于 80 °C 才是气体。20 °C 低于沸点。

mixture.en: Mixture is about what a substance is made of, not its state. The question asks the state.
mixture.zh: 混合物讲的是组成，不是状态。题目问的是状态。

questions.qzh: 一种物质在 -10 °C 熔化，在 80 °C 沸腾。在 20 °C 时它是……

questions.q: In a fair test, the variables you keep the SAME are the...

why.en: C-M-S: Change one, Measure one, keep the rest the Same (control).
why.zh: C-M-S：改变一个，测量一个，其他保持不变（控制变量）。

independent variable.en: The independent variable is the ONE thing you CHANGE.
independent variable.zh: 自变量是你改变的那一样。

dependent variable.en: The dependent variable is what you MEASURE.
dependent variable.zh: 因变量是你测量的东西。

results.en: Results are the measurements you record, not variables you hold steady.
results.zh: 结果是记录的测量值，不是保持不变的变量。

questions.qzh: 在公平测试里，保持不变的变量叫……

canNow.en: I can still answer the chemistry questions by myself.
canNow.zh: 我仍然能自己回答化学题。

title.en: Monday Homework: Refraction and Colour (B6, B7)
title.zh: 星期一作业：折射和颜色（B6、B7）

subtitle.en: 12 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Read Main Book B6 and B7 first. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 B6 和 B7。可以做很多次。

questions.q: Refraction is when light changes direction because its ___ changes.

why.en: Light travels at different speeds in different materials (fastest in air, slower in glass or water). When it enters a new material at an angle, the change in SPEED makes it change direction: refraction.
why.zh: 光在不同物质中速度不同（空气中最快，玻璃和水中较慢）。斜着进入新物质时，速度改变让它改变方向：折射。

colour.en: The colour stays the same when light enters a new material.
colour.zh: 光进入新物质时颜色不变。

amplitude.en: Amplitude is about brightness and does not bend light.
amplitude.zh: 振幅关系到亮度，不会让光弯折。

source.en: The source stays the same. The new MATERIAL changes the speed.
source.zh: 光源没变，是新的物质改变了速度。

questions.qzh: 折射是光因为 ___ 改变而改变方向。

questions.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent. This is caused by...

why.en: Light from the straw bends (refracts) as it leaves the water and enters the air, because it speeds up. Your eyes assume light travels straight, so the straw looks broken.
why.zh: 从吸管来的光离开水进入空气时会弯折（折射），因为速度变快了。眼睛以为光是直线走的，所以吸管看起来断了。

reflection.en: Reflection is light bouncing back. The light here passes OUT of the water and bends.
reflection.zh: 反射是光弹回来。这里的光是穿出水面并弯折。

dispersion.en: Dispersion splits white light into colours. The straw does not turn into a rainbow.
dispersion.zh: 色散是把白光分成颜色。吸管不会变成彩虹。

absorption.en: Absorption takes light in. It does not make things look bent.
absorption.zh: 吸收是把光吸进去，不会让东西看起来弯。

questions.qzh: 吸管放在水杯里看起来弯了。这是由……造成的。

questions.q: A prism splits white light into colours. This is...

why.en: Dispersion = separating white light into colours.
why.zh: 色散 = 白光分成各种颜色。

reflection.en: Reflection bounces light back; it does not separate the colours.
reflection.zh: 反射把光弹回来，不会把颜色分开。

lateral inversion.en: Lateral inversion is a mirror swapping left and right.
lateral inversion.zh: 左右颠倒是镜子把左右换过来。

absorption.en: Absorption takes light in. A prism lets the light through and spreads it out.
absorption.zh: 吸收是把光吸进去。棱镜是让光通过并分散开。

questions.qzh: 棱镜把白光分成各种颜色。这是……

questions.q: A prism is usually made of...

why.en: A prism must let light pass THROUGH it (transparent), so it is made of clear glass or plastic.
why.zh: 棱镜必须让光穿过（透明），所以用透明的玻璃或塑料做。

wood.en: Wood is opaque: no light passes through, so it cannot split light.
wood.zh: 木头不透明，光穿不过，所以不能分光。

metal.en: Metal is opaque and reflects light instead.

paper.en: Paper is opaque or translucent, so light cannot pass cleanly through it.
paper.zh: 纸不透明或半透明，光不能清楚地穿过。

questions.qzh: 棱镜通常用……做成。

questions.q: The visible spectrum is a range of...

why.en: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.
why.zh: 红、橙、黄、绿、蓝、靛、紫。

sounds.en: Sounds have a range of frequencies too, but the VISIBLE spectrum is light we can see.
sounds.zh: 声音也有频率范围，但“可见”光谱是我们能看见的光。

temperatures.en: Temperatures are measured with a thermometer, not seen as a spectrum.
temperatures.zh: 温度用温度计测量，不是光谱。

mirrors.en: Mirrors reflect light; they are not part of the spectrum.
mirrors.zh: 镜子反射光，不是光谱的一部分。

questions.qzh: 可见光谱是一系列……

questions.q: The primary colours of light are...

why.en: For light: red, green, blue.
why.zh: 光的三原色：红、绿、蓝。

red, yellow and blue.en: Red, yellow and blue are the primary colours of PAINT. Light ADDS colours, and its primaries are red, green and blue.
red, yellow and blue.zh: 红、黄、蓝是颜料的三原色。光是颜色相加，原色是红、绿、蓝。

cyan, magenta and yellow.en: These are the SECONDARY colours of light.

black and white.en: Black is no light, and white is all colours together. Neither is a primary colour.
black and white.zh: 黑是没有光，白是所有颜色加在一起，都不是原色。

questions.qzh: 光的三原色是……

questions.q: Green light + blue light = ?

why.en: Adding coloured light: green + blue = cyan (a light blue-green).
why.zh: 光的颜色相加：绿 + 蓝 = 青色（浅蓝绿色）。

white.en: White needs all three: red + green + blue.
white.zh: 白光要三种都有：红 + 绿 + 蓝。

questions.qzh: 绿光 + 蓝光 = ？

questions.q: Red light + green light + blue light = ?

why.en: Adding all three primary colours of light (red, green and blue) gives white light. That is how screens make white.
why.zh: 光的三原色（红、绿、蓝）全部加在一起就是白光，屏幕就是这样显示白色的。

black.en: Black is NO light at all. Adding light makes it brighter, not darker.
black.zh: 黑是完全没有光。加光只会更亮，不会更暗。

brown.en: Brown comes from mixing PAINTS, which absorb light. Lights add together.
brown.zh: 棕色是颜料混合出来的，颜料会吸收光。光是相加的。

yellow.en: Yellow is only red + green. Adding blue too makes white.
yellow.zh: 黄色只是红 + 绿。再加上蓝就是白。

questions.qzh: 红光 + 绿光 + 蓝光 = ？

questions.q: A green leaf looks green because it...
options: reflects green light and absorbs the rest

why.en: We see the colour that is reflected.
why.zh: 我们看到的是被反射的颜色。

absorbs green light.en: If it absorbed green, no green would reach your eyes. We see the colour that is REFLECTED.
absorbs green light.zh: 如果吸收了绿光，就没有绿光进入眼睛。我们看到的是被反射的颜色。

makes green light.en: A leaf is non-luminous; it does not glow in the dark.
makes green light.zh: 叶子不发光，在黑暗里不会亮。

transmits all light.en: If all light passed through, the leaf would look clear, not green.
transmits all light.zh: 如果所有光都穿过去，叶子会是透明的，不是绿色。

questions.qzh: 绿叶看起来是绿色的，因为它……

ozh.reflects green light and absorbs the res: 反射绿光，吸收其他颜色

questions.q: A white T-shirt looks white because it...

why.en: White reflects every colour.
why.zh: 白色反射所有颜色。

absorbs all colours.en: Absorbing all colours makes something look BLACK.
absorbs all colours.zh: 吸收所有颜色的东西看起来是黑色的。

makes its own light.en: A T-shirt is non-luminous; it does not glow.

is transparent.en: A transparent T-shirt would be see-through, not white.
is transparent.zh: 透明的 T 恤是能看穿的，不是白色。

questions.qzh: 白 T 恤看起来是白色的，因为它……

questions.q: A black T-shirt looks black because it...

why.en: Black absorbs every colour, so no light reaches your eye.
why.zh: 黑色吸收所有颜色，没有光进入眼睛。

reflects all colours.en: Reflecting all colours makes something look WHITE.
reflects all colours.zh: 反射所有颜色的东西看起来是白色的。

reflects only black light.en: There is no "black light" colour in white light. Black is the absence of reflected light.
reflects only black light.zh: 白光里没有“黑光”。黑色就是没有反射的光。

is luminous.en: A black T-shirt makes no light, and if it did it would not look black.
is luminous.zh: 黑 T 恤不发光，如果发光就不会是黑的。

questions.qzh: 黑 T 恤看起来是黑色的，因为它……

questions.q: To transmit light means to...

why.en: Transmit = allow light to pass through a material.
why.zh: 透射 = 让光穿过材料。

questions.qzh: transmit（透射）光的意思是……

canNow.en: I can now explain refraction, dispersion and why objects have colours.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释折射、色散，以及物体为什么有颜色。

title.en: Day 1: Elements, Compounds, Particles and Counting Atoms
title.zh: 第 1 天：元素、化合物、粒子图和数原子
第 2 页：元素、化合物还是混合物？

items.q: Oxygen (O₂): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: One capital letter, so one kind of atom: element.
why.zh: 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子：元素。

items.q: Carbon dioxide (CO₂): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Two capital letters (C and O) chemically joined in one formula: compound.
why.zh: 两个大写字母 C 和 O 结合在一个化学式里：化合物。

items.q: Air: element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Air is many gases (nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide...) mixed together, not joined.
why.zh: 空气是很多种气体（氮气、氧气、二氧化碳……）混在一起，没有结合。

items.q: Magnesium (Mg): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: One capital letter, so one kind of atom: element.
why.zh: 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子：元素。

items.q: Sodium chloride (NaCl): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Sodium and chlorine are chemically joined. That is salt, a compound.
why.zh: 钠和氯化学结合在一起，就是盐，是化合物。

items.q: Brass: element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Brass is an alloy: copper and zinc melted and mixed, not chemically joined. Alloys are mixtures.
why.zh: 黄铜是合金：铜和锌熔化后混在一起，没有化学结合。合金是混合物。

items.q: Carbon monoxide (CO): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: C and O are two capital letters: two kinds of atom joined. (Co with a small o would be cobalt, an element.)
why.zh: C 和 O 是两个大写字母：两种原子结合。（小写 o 的 Co 是钴，是元素。）

items.q: Petrol: element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Petrol has no single formula. It is many substances mixed together.
why.zh: 汽油没有一个化学式，是很多物质混在一起。

items.q: Which of these is a compound? a) carbon monoxide b) magnesium c) bromine d) brass

why.en: CO = two kinds of atom joined. Magnesium and bromine are elements; brass is a mixture.
why.zh: CO = 两种原子结合。镁和溴是元素，黄铜是混合物。

items.q: Which of these is an element? a) MgS b) NaCl c) CoO d) O₂

why.en: O₂ has one capital letter. MgS, NaCl and CoO each have two kinds of atom.
why.zh: O₂ 只有一个大写字母。MgS、NaCl 和 CoO 都有两种原子。

items.q: Which order matches: hydrogen, petrol, water?

why.en: Hydrogen = element, petrol = mixture, water (H₂O) = compound.
why.zh: 氢 = 元素，汽油 = 混合物，水 (H₂O) = 化合物。

items.q: Fill the gaps: Atoms are the smallest parts of ___. Same atoms join: a ___ is formed. Different atoms join: they form ___.
Draw 2 atoms of the SAME colour joined. Element or compound?

why.en: Same colour = same kind of atom, so it is an element (a molecule of an element, like O₂).
why.zh: 颜色相同 = 同一种原子，所以是元素（元素的分子，比如 O₂）。

label.zh: 样例：2 个相同原子结合 = 元素

items.q: Draw 2 atoms of DIFFERENT colours joined. Element or compound?

why.en: Different colours joined = different atoms chemically joined = compound.
why.zh: 不同颜色结合 = 不同原子化学结合 = 化合物。

label.zh: 样例：2 个不同原子结合 = 化合物

items.q: Box A: red-blue pairs and single blue atoms. Name the box.
items.right: mixture of an element and a compound

why.en: Red-blue pairs = different atoms joined = compound. Single blue atoms = element. Together: a mixture of an element and a compound.
why.zh: 红蓝一对 = 不同原子结合 = 化合物。单个蓝原子 = 元素。合起来：元素和化合物的混合物。

items.q: Box B: only blue-blue pairs. Name the box.

why.en: Every particle is the same: two blue atoms joined. Same atoms = element; joined = molecules.
why.zh: 每个粒子都一样：两个蓝原子结合。相同原子 = 元素；结合 = 分子。

items.q: Box C: blue-blue pairs and single red atoms. Name the box.

why.en: Blue-blue = an element. Single red atoms = another element. Not joined to each other: a mixture of two elements.
why.zh: 蓝蓝 = 一种元素，单个红原子 = 另一种元素，彼此没有结合：两种元素的混合物。

items.q: Box D: single yellow atoms only. Name the box.

why.en: One kind of atom, not joined: an element made of single atoms.
why.zh: 只有一种原子，没有结合：由单个原子组成的元素。

items.q: Box E: all particles are the same 3-atom molecule (yellow-red-yellow). Name the box.

why.en: All particles the same (pure), and each has different atoms joined: compound.
why.zh: 所有粒子都一样（纯净物），每个粒子里不同原子结合：化合物。

items.q: Box F: yellow-red-yellow molecules and blue-blue pairs. Name the box.
items.right: mixture of an element and a compound

why.en: Yellow-red-yellow = compound. Blue-blue = same atoms = element. So: a mixture of an element and a compound.
why.zh: 黄红黄 = 化合物。蓝蓝 = 相同原子 = 元素。所以是元素和化合物的混合物。

items.q: Draw a mixture of two elements.
items.right: two kinds of element particle, not joined to each other

label.zh: 样例：两种元素的混合物

items.q: Draw THREE water molecules (H₂O).
items.right: three molecules, each one O joined to two H

why.en: H₂O = 1 oxygen + 2 hydrogen joined. Three molecules = three of these groups (9 atoms).
why.zh: H₂O = 1 个氧 + 2 个氢结合。三个分子 = 三组（一共 9 个原子）。

items.q: Draw a mixture of an element and a compound.
items.right: some same-colour pairs (element) AND some different-colour pairs (compound)

why.en: You need both kinds: same-colour particles for the element and different-colour joined particles for the compound.
why.zh: 两种都要有：颜色相同的粒子是元素，颜色不同结合的粒子是化合物。

items.q: Red and blue atoms in a box, NOT touching. Mixture or compound?

why.en: Not touching = not joined = mixture.
why.zh: 没有碰在一起 = 没有结合 = 混合物。

label.zh: 没有碰在一起 = 混合物

items.q: CO₂: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: H₂O₂: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: NaCl: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: NH₃: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: H₂SO₄: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: C₆H₁₂O₆: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: How many atoms in 4 molecules of CO₂?

why.en: One CO₂ has 3 atoms. 4 molecules × 3 atoms = 12 atoms.
why.zh: 一个 CO₂ 有 3 个原子。4 个分子 × 3 = 12 个原子。

items.q: How many HYDROGEN atoms in 5 molecules of CH₄?

why.en: One CH₄ has 4 hydrogen atoms. 5 × 4 = 20.
why.zh: 一个 CH₄ 有 4 个氢原子。5 × 4 = 20。

items.q: A molecule has 1 carbon atom and 4 hydrogen atoms. Write its formula.

why.en: C for carbon, H for hydrogen, small 4 after H.
why.zh: C 是碳，H 是氢，H 后面写小的 4。

items.q: Hydrogen peroxide picture (O-O in the middle, H at each end). Formula?

why.en: 2 hydrogen + 2 oxygen atoms = H₂O₂.
why.zh: 2 个氢 + 2 个氧 = H₂O₂。

label.en: H₂O₂: H, O, O, H joined

items.q: Cryolite puzzle: Al = 1, Na = 3 × Al, F = 2 × Na. Formula?

title.en: Day 2: Word Equations, Iron and Sulfur, Negative Numbers
title.zh: 第 2 天：文字方程式、铁和硫、负数
第 5 页：化学反应和文字方程式

items.q: lead + ___ → lead sulfide

why.en: Lead sulfide is made from lead and sulfur. On the left side, write the element's own name: sulfur. The word "sulfide" is only for the new compound on the right.
why.zh: 硫化铅是由铅和硫生成的。左边写元素本来的名字：sulfur（硫）。sulfide 这个词只用在右边生成的新化合物里。

items.q: copper + chlorine → ___

why.en: Chlorine → chloride. Small spelling tip: chloride has one L after the H: c-h-l-o-r-i-d-e.
why.zh: chlorine → chloride。拼写小提示：c-h-l-o-r-i-d-e。

items.q: zinc + sulfur → ___

why.en: Keep the metal name; the non-metal changes its ending to -ide.
why.zh: 金属名字不变；非金属结尾改成 -ide。

items.q: iron + oxygen → ___

why.en: Oxygen → oxide.
why.zh: oxygen → oxide。

items.q: ___ + oxygen → magnesium oxide

why.en: The metal name stays the same on both sides.
why.zh: 金属名字两边一样。

items.q: sodium + ___ → sodium chloride

why.en: Chloride comes from chlorine. Spelling tip: c-h-l-o-r-i-n-e (don't forget the L).
why.zh: chloride 来自 chlorine。拼写：c-h-l-o-r-i-n-e（别忘了 L）。

items.q: Challenge: sulfur + oxygen → ___ (the product is SO₂)

why.en: SO₂ has TWO oxygen atoms. Two = di, so: sulfur dioxide.
why.zh: SO₂ 有两个氧原子。二 = di，所以是 sulfur dioxide。

items.q: Which reaction is: compound → two elements?

why.en: Water is ONE compound. It splits into TWO elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
why.zh: 水是一种化合物，分解成两种元素：氢和氧。

items.q: Which reaction is: element + element → compound?

why.en: Zinc and sulfur are both elements, and they join to make one compound.
why.zh: 锌和硫都是元素，结合成一种化合物。

items.q: BEFORE (2 H₂ and 1 O₂) is a mixture of two ___.

why.en: H₂ and O₂ are both elements, just mixed.
why.zh: H₂ 和 O₂ 都是元素，只是混在一起。

items.q: AFTER (2 H₂O) is a ___.

why.en: Water has H and O joined: a compound. Atoms before = 6, atoms after = 6. Atoms are never lost!
why.zh: 水里 H 和 O 结合：化合物。反应前 6 个原子，反应后也是 6 个。原子不会消失！

title.en: Page 6: The Iron and Sulfur Story
title.zh: 第 6 页：铁和硫的故事

items.q: Give ONE way you can tell a chemical reaction took place.
items.right: e.g. it glowed brightly / a black solid formed / the colour changed

why.en: Signs of a reaction: light or heat given out, colour change, a gas, or a new substance with new properties.
why.zh: 化学反应的迹象：发光或放热、颜色改变、产生气体、或生成有新性质的新物质。

items.q: Iron: metallic element, non-metallic element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Iron is a metal and only one kind of atom (Fe).
why.zh: 铁是金属，只有一种原子 (Fe)。

items.q: Sulfur: metallic element, non-metallic element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Sulfur is a yellow non-metal, one kind of atom (S).
why.zh: 硫是黄色的非金属，只有一种原子 (S)。

items.q: Iron sulfide: metallic element, non-metallic element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Iron and sulfur chemically joined after heating.
why.zh: 加热后铁和硫化学结合。

items.q: Iron + sulfur before heating: ?

why.en: Before heating they are just mixed. A magnet can still pull the iron out.
why.zh: 加热前只是混在一起，磁铁还能把铁吸出来。

items.q: Is iron magnetic?

why.en: Iron is one of the few magnetic metals.
why.zh: 铁是少数有磁性的金属之一。

items.q: Is sulfur magnetic?

why.en: Sulfur is a non-metal and not magnetic.
why.zh: 硫是非金属，没有磁性。

items.q: Is iron sulfide magnetic?

why.en: Iron sulfide is a NEW substance with new properties. It is not magnetic.
why.zh: 硫化亚铁是新物质，有新的性质，没有磁性。

items.q: Zinc is heated with sulfur. Name the solid that forms.

why.en: Keep the metal name (zinc) + sulfur becomes sulfide: zinc sulfide.
why.zh: 金属名字不变（zinc）+ sulfur 变成 sulfide：zinc sulfide。

items.q: Name TWO compounds from: calcium carbonate, iron, sulfur, carbon dioxide, chlorine.

why.en: Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) both have different atoms joined. Iron, sulfur and chlorine are elements.
why.zh: 碳酸钙 (CaCO₃) 和二氧化碳 (CO₂) 都是不同原子结合。铁、硫、氯是元素。

items.q: Is iron sulfide the same as the iron and sulfur mixture? Explain using a magnet.
items.right: No. A magnet pulls iron out of the mixture, but not out of iron sulfide, because the iron is joined to sulfur in a new substance.

why.en: Mixture = not joined, so the magnet separates them. Compound = joined, so the magnet cannot.
why.zh: 混合物 = 没有结合，所以磁铁能分开；化合物 = 结合了，所以磁铁分不开。

items.q: Melting chocolate: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Still chocolate, and it can set again.
why.zh: 还是巧克力，还能再凝固。

items.q: Dissolving sugar in water: physical or chemical change?

why.en: No new substance. Boil off the water and the sugar is still there.
why.zh: 没有新物质。把水煮干，糖还在。

items.q: Boiling water: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Water becomes steam and can turn back into water.
why.zh: 水变成水蒸气，还能变回水。

items.q: Cooking an egg: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Cooking makes new substances in the egg, and you cannot make it raw again.
why.zh: 煮鸡蛋生成了新物质，鸡蛋变不回生的。

items.q: Rusting iron: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Iron joins with oxygen and water to make rust, a new substance.
why.zh: 铁和氧、水结合生成铁锈，是新物质。

items.q: Burning paper: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Burning makes ash and gases. You cannot get the paper back.
why.zh: 燃烧生成灰和气体，纸变不回来。

items.q: Which element is a liquid at 0 °C?

why.en: Mercury melts at -39 °C and boils at 357 °C. 0 is in between, so it is a liquid.
why.zh: 汞的熔点是 -39 °C，沸点是 357 °C。0 在中间，所以是液体。

items.q: Which element is a solid at 1500 °C?

why.en: Iron melts at 1540 °C. 1500 is colder than that, so iron is still solid.
why.zh: 铁的熔点是 1540 °C。1500 比它低，所以铁还是固体。

items.q: Which element is a gas at 2000 °C?

why.en: Magnesium boils at 1100 °C, so at 2000 °C it is a gas. Mercury is a gas too.
why.zh: 镁的沸点是 1100 °C，所以 2000 °C 时是气体。汞也是气体。

items.q: Which TWO elements are liquids at 1000 °C?

why.en: Aluminium: 660 to 2520 °C. Magnesium: 650 to 1100 °C. 1000 is inside both ranges.

items.q: Put in order, smallest first: 12, -39, 0, -100, -5

why.en: All negative numbers are smaller than 0. Further from 0 on the left = smaller.
why.zh: 所有负数都比 0 小。在数轴上离 0 越远（左边）越小。

why.en: Start at 3 and go down 10 steps: -7.
why.zh: 从 3 往下走 10 步：-7。

why.en: Start at -4 and go up 9 steps: 5.
why.zh: 从 -4 往上走 9 步：5。

why.en: Start at -6 and go down 4 more: -10.
why.zh: 从 -6 再往下走 4 步：-10。

why.en: Up 2 from -2 lands on 0.
why.zh: 从 -2 往上 2 步正好到 0。

items.q: The temperature goes from -5 °C to 8 °C. How many degrees did it go up?

why.en: 5 degrees up to 0, then 8 more: 13 °C.
why.zh: 先升 5 度到 0，再升 8 度：13 °C。

items.q: Mercury melts at -39 °C and boils at 357 °C. How many degrees between them?

why.en: 357 - (-39) = 357 + 39 = 396 °C. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

items.q: Iron 2.0 g → iron sulfide 2.8 g. How much did the mass increase?
Why did the mass go up? Use the word sulfur.
items.right: Because 0.8 g of sulfur joined the iron.

why.en: The iron did not get heavier by itself. Sulfur atoms joined on, so the mass went up.
why.zh: 铁自己不会变重。是硫原子结合上去，所以质量增加了。

items.q: 5.0 g magnesium → 8.3 g magnesium oxide. How much oxygen joined?

why.en: Oxygen from the air joined on: 8.3 - 5.0 = 3.3 g.
why.zh: 空气中的氧结合上去：8.3 - 5.0 = 3.3 克。

title.en: Day 3: States of Matter, Fair Test, Ratio
title.zh: 第 3 天：物态、公平实验、比
第 8 页：固体、液体和气体

items.q: Draw about 12 particles for a liquid and a gas.
items.right: liquid: close, random; gas: far apart

items.q: Draw about 12 particles for a SOLID.

why.en: Solid particles are close together in NEAT ROWS, like students sitting in class.
why.zh: 固体粒子紧紧排成整齐的行，像学生坐在教室里。

items.q: solid → liquid is called?

why.en: Solid to liquid = melting.
why.zh: 固体变液体 = 熔化。

items.q: liquid → gas is called?

why.en: Liquid to gas = boiling.
why.zh: 液体变气体 = 沸腾。

items.q: liquid → solid is called?

why.en: Liquid to solid = freezing.
why.zh: 液体变固体 = 凝固。

items.q: gas → liquid is called?

why.en: Gas back to liquid = condensing (like water drops on a cold glass).
why.zh: 气体变回液体 = 凝结（像冷杯子外的水珠）。

items.q: Which statement about liquids is correct?
items.right: c) no fixed shape, but a fixed volume

why.en: A liquid takes the shape of its container but keeps its volume.
why.zh: 液体形状随容器变，但体积不变。

items.q: Particles change from regular (neat rows) to random. Which process?

why.en: Solid (neat rows) → liquid (random) = melting.
why.zh: 固体（整齐）→ 液体（无序）= 熔化。

items.q: Which TWO words apply to nitrogen?

why.en: Nitrogen (N₂) is a gas in the air, and it has only one kind of atom: element.
why.zh: 氮气 (N₂) 是空气里的气体，只有一种原子：元素。

items.q: Which TWO words apply to copper sulfate (blue crystals, CuSO₄)?

why.en: Crystals are solid; Cu, S and O are joined: compound.
why.zh: 晶体是固体；Cu、S、O 结合：化合物。

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.right: b) There are 2 liquid elements at room temperature.

why.en: Mercury and bromine are the two liquid elements at room temperature.
why.zh: 汞和溴是室温下的两种液态元素。

title.en: Page 9: Planning an Investigation (Priestley and Lavoisier)
title.zh: 第 9 页：设计实验（Priestley 和 Lavoisier）

items.q: Priestley and Lavoisier: what is the ONE thing you will change?

why.en: The independent variable is the ONE thing you change: here, the type of metal.
why.zh: 自变量是你改变的那一个东西：这里是金属的种类。

items.q: What will you measure?

why.en: The dependent variable is what you measure: the mass.
why.zh: 因变量是你测量的东西：质量。

items.q: What will you keep the same?
items.right: the same starting mass of metal, the same heating time, the same crucible

why.en: Control variables keep the test fair: same starting mass, same heating time, same crucible.
why.zh: 控制变量让实验公平：相同的起始质量、相同的加热时间、相同的坩埚。

items.q: What do you think will happen to the mass? Why?
items.right: the mass will increase because the metal gains oxygen from the air

items.q: Draw a results table.
items.right: metal | mass before (g) | mass after (g) | change in mass (g)

why.en: First column = what you change. Put units (g) in the headings.
why.zh: 第一列 = 你改变的东西。表头里写上单位 (g)。

main.en: metal | mass before (g) | mass after (g) | change in mass (g)
main.zh: 金属 | 加热前质量 (g) | 加热后质量 (g) | 质量变化 (g)

example.en: one row for each of the 3 metals

items.q: Who is right: Priestley or Lavoisier?

why.en: The mass went UP after heating, so the metal gained something from the air. That is Lavoisier's idea.
why.zh: 加热后质量增加了，说明金属从空气中得到了东西。这是 Lavoisier 的观点。

items.q: Magnesium 2.4 g → magnesium oxide 4.0 g. How much oxygen joined?

why.en: 4.0 - 2.4 = 1.6 g of oxygen joined.

items.q: Ratio of carbon : oxygen in CO₂?

why.en: Follow the ORDER of the words: carbon first (1), then oxygen (2).
why.zh: 按词的顺序：先碳 (1)，再氧 (2)。

items.q: 6 molecules of CO₂: how many carbon atoms?
6 molecules of CO₂: how many oxygen atoms?

why.en: Each CO₂ has 2 oxygen atoms: 6 × 2 = 12.
why.zh: 每个 CO₂ 有 2 个氧原子：6 × 2 = 12。

items.q: Simplify the ratio 4 : 2.

why.en: Divide both numbers by 2.
why.zh: 两个数都除以 2。

items.q: Simplify the ratio 6 : 9.

why.en: Divide both numbers by 3.
why.zh: 两个数都除以 3。

items.q: Ratio of Na : Al : F in Na₃AlF₆?

why.en: Read the small numbers in order: Na 3, Al 1 (no number), F 6.
why.zh: 按顺序读小数字：Na 3，Al 1（没有数字），F 6。

items.q: 24 + x = 40. Find x.

why.en: Do the opposite: take away 24 from both sides. 40 - 24 = 16. Check: 24 + 16 = 40 ✓

items.q: 3x = 12. Find x.

why.en: Divide both sides by 3.
why.zh: 两边都除以 3。

items.q: x ÷ 2 = 7. Find x.

why.en: Multiply both sides by 2.
why.zh: 两边都乘 2。

items.q: 2x + 3 = 11. Find x.

why.en: Take away 3 (8), then divide by 2 (4).
why.zh: 先减 3（得 8），再除以 2（得 4）。
